### Learn with Our Institution

In order to provide meritorious education with a commitment to Excellence and find opportunity to apply the knowledge and skills in the industry as well as in the society we live.

### IEI

The Institution of Engineers (India), the IEI, is a national organization for engineers in India. It is the world’s largest multi-disciplinary engineering professional society. It has more than one million members in 15 engineering disciplines. The institution was established in 1920 in Kolkata, West Bengal, and was incorporated by royal charter in 1935.

#### About IEI at AACET

The Institution of Engineers (India) at AAA College of Engineering and Technology (AACET) was established in 2026 with the objective of promoting technical competence and professional excellence among students. The chapter is affiliated with Institution of Engineers (India), a nationally recognized professional body dedicated to the advancement of engineering and technology.

The IEI Students’ Chapter at AACET provides a vibrant platform for students to explore emerging technologies, engage in professional activities, and develop industry-relevant skills.

#### IEI Student Forum at AACET

The IEI Student Forum functions as an active student-driven body under the IEI Chapter, organizing various academic and co-curricular activities. It encourages innovation, leadership, and collaboration among students across all engineering disciplines.

#### Objectives

- To bridge the gap between academic curriculum and industry expectations.

- To organize technical seminars, workshops, and guest lectures.

- To promote participation in IEI events, competitions, and certifications.

- To foster teamwork, communication, and professional ethics

- To create awareness about emerging technologies and engineering practices.

Key Activities

- Technical Workshops and Hands-on Training Programs.

- Guest Lectures by Industry Experts and Academicians.

- National and International Webinars.

- Industrial Visits and Field Trips.

- Technical Quiz, Paper Presentation, and Project Expo.

- Skill Development and Career Guidance Programs.

Benefits of IEI Membership

- Access to technical journals and IEI publications.

- Opportunities to participate in national-level IEI events.

- Networking with professional engineers and industry experts.

- Exposure to real-world engineering challenges.

- Enhancement of employability and career prospects.

### IETE

The Institution of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineers (IETE) is India’s leading recognised professional society devoted to the advancement of Science and Technology of Electronics, Telecommunication & IT. Founded in 1953.

##### IETE Students' Forum Background

The Institution of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineers (IETE) is India’s leading recognised professional society devoted to the advancement of Science and Technology of Electronics, Telecommunication & IT. Founded in 1953, the IETE is the National Apex Professional body of Electronics and Telecommunication, Computer Science and IT Professionals. It serves more than 1,25,000 members (including Corporate, Student and ISF members) through various 64 Centres, spread all over India and abroad. The Institution provides leadership in Scientific and Technical areas of direct importance to the national development and economy.

Government of India has recognized IETE as a Scientific and Industrial Research Organization (SIRO) and also notified as an educational Institution of national eminence. The objectives of IETE focus on advancing electro-technology. The IETE conducts and sponsors technical meetings, conferences, symposia, and exhibitions all over India, publishes technical journals and provides continuing education as well as career advancement opportunities to its members.

The IETE focuses on advancement of the Science and Technology of Electronics, Telecommunication, Computers, Information Technology and related areas. Towards this end the Institution promotes and conducts basic engineering and continuing technical education programmes for human resource development.

##### Objectives of ISF

- Improving standard of Engineering Education.

- Counselling the students in the emerging new opportunitie

- Encouraging and motivating outside classroom studies through workshops, projects, seminars, and technical activities.

- Increasing the student base and Corporate Membership of IETE.

##### IETE at AAACET

The IETE – Students’ Forum (ISF) was started in AAA College of Engineering and Technology in the year 2015. Since then, the ISF has been actively conducting various events such as symposiums, technical seminars, workshops, guest lectures, and other professional development activities for students.

### IQAC

The IQAC, or Internal Quality Assurance Cell, at our institution plays a crucial role in ensuring and enhancing the quality of education and overall functioning of our organization.

#### Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC)

As per the guidelines of National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC), the establishment of Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) is a mandatory requirement for all NAAC-accredited institutions. AAA College of Engineering and Technology, (AAACET) has been recently accredited in 2021 with the grade A (3.15/4.0) by NAAC (National Assessment and Accreditation Council) for the period 23.02.2021 – 22.02.2026.

The IQAC at AAACET has been consistently and actively involved in quality sustenance and enhancement activities. It is a participative cell that works on evolving strategies to remove deficiencies, stay receptive to changes and enhance quality, thus channelizing the efforts of the stakeholders at AAACET towards achieving holistic academic excellence, generating desired educational outcomes and delivering on best student-life experiences.

#### OBJECTIVES

- To develop a system for conscious, consistent and catalytic action to improve the academic and administrative performance of the Institution.

- To promote measures for the institutional functioning towards quality enhancement through internalization of quality culture and institutionalization of best practices.

#### STRATEGIES

IQAC shall evolve mechanisms and procedures for:

- Ensuring timely, efficient and progressive performance of academic, administrative and financial tasks

- The relevance and quality of academic and research programmes

- Equitable access to and affordability of academic programmes for various sections of society

- Optimization and integration of modern methods of teaching and learning

- The credibility of evaluation procedures

- Ensuring the adequacy, maintenance and functioning of the support structure and services

- Research sharing and networking with other institutions in India and abroad

#### FUNCTIONS

- Development and application of quality benchmarks/parameters for various academic and administrative activities of the institution

- Facilitating the creation of a learner-centric environment conducive to quality education and faculty maturation to adopt the required knowledge and technology for participatory teaching and learning process

- Arrangement for feedback response from students, parents and other stakeholders on quality-related institutional processes

- Dissemination of information on various quality parameters of higher education

- Organization of inter and intra institutional workshops, seminars on quality related themes and promotion of quality circles

- Documentation of the various programmes/activities leading to quality improvement

- Acting as a nodal agency of the Institution for coordinating quality-related activities, including adoption and dissemination of best practices

- Development and maintenance of institutional database through MIS for the purpose of maintaining/enhancing the institutional quality Development of Quality Culture in the institution

- Preparation of the Annual Quality Assurance Report (AQAR) as per guidelines and parameters of NAAC, to be submitted to NAAC

#### BENEFITS

IQAC will facilitate/contribute:

- Ensure heightened level of clarity and focus in institutional functioning towards quality enhancement Ensure internalization of the quality culture

- Ensure enhancement and coordination among various activities of the institution and institutionalize all good practices

- Provide a sound basis for decision-making to improve institutional functioning

- Act as a dynamic system for quality changes in HEIs

- Build an organised methodology of documentation and internal communication

### ICI

The Indian Concrete Institute (ICI) Professional Chapter in the Civil Engineering Department connects academic learning with industry practices in concrete technology and structural engineering.
It promotes technical excellence, innovation, and professional ethics among students and faculty.
The chapter organizes workshops, seminars, guest lectures, and industrial visits.
It also enables interaction with industry experts and practicing engineers.

Indian Concrete Institute (ICI) – Professional Chapter

Institutional Membership Details AAA College of Engineering and Technology holds an Organization Life Membership with the Indian Concrete Institute (ICI). Membership Number: 15401 ICI Centre: Madurai Centre (Centre Code: MADC)

About the ICI Chapter

The Indian Concrete Institute (ICI) Professional Chapter in the Department of Civil Engineering serves as a platform to bridge the gap between academic learning and industry practices in concrete technology, construction materials, and structural engineering. The chapter promotes technical excellence, innovation, and professional ethics through various academic and industry-oriented activities.

It provides opportunities for students and faculty to interact with industry experts and practicing engineers through regular programmes such as workshops, seminars, guest lectures, and industrial visits.

Objectives

- To enhance knowledge in concrete technology, structural engineering, and modern construction practices

- To create interaction opportunities with industry experts, researchers, and professionals

- To organize technical programmes such as workshops, seminars, and industrial visits

- To develop employability skills, leadership qualities, and professional ethics among students

Outcomes

- Improved practical knowledge in materials testing, mix design, and construction techniques

- Enhanced technical competency and industry readiness among students

- Increased participation in professional, research, and technical activities

- Better career opportunities through industry exposure and networking

Future Plans

- Organize regular guest lectures by eminent professionals from the construction industry

- Conduct advanced training programmes on concrete mix design, NDT techniques, BIM, and smart construction technologies

- Establish student technical clubs under the ICI Chapter for innovation and project development

- Collaborate with industries for internships, consultancy works, and sponsored projects

- Host state-level and national-level technical symposiums, paper presentations, and design contests

- Encourage faculty and students to publish research papers in concrete and structural engineering domains

- Promote green concrete technologies, waste material utilization, and sustainable infrastructure practices

- Strengthen industry–academia partnerships for continuous skill enhancement and career opportunities

### FACEAT

The Federation of All Civil Engineering Association of Tamil Nadu & Pondicherry (FACEAT) is established with the vision of uniting all civil engineering professionals, practitioners, and associations across the regions of Tamil Nadu and Pondicherry.

##### FACEAT CHAPTER

The Federation of All Civil Engineering Association of Tamil Nadu & Pondicherry (FACEAT) is established with the vision of uniting all civil engineering professionals, practitioners, and associations across the regions of Tamil Nadu and Pondicherry. This federation strives to foster collaboration, promote innovation, and elevate the standards of civil engineering in the region. By encouraging knowledge exchange, supporting the professional growth of civil engineers, and addressing the challenges faced by the community, FACEAT aims to contribute significantly to the development of sustainable infrastructure and built environments. FACEAT Establishment Year: 2024

##### OBJECTIVE

- To serve as an umbrella organization that brings together all civil engineering associations across Tamil Nadu and Pondicherry.

- To facilitate the continuous professional development of civil engineers through seminars, workshops, and technical training programs.

- To encourage the adoption of innovative technologies and industry best practices to improve the efficiency and quality of civil engineering projects.

- To represent the interests of civil engineers at the governmental level and advocate for policies that benefit the profession and contribute to sustainable development.

- To promote collaboration between educational institutions, industry, and government to align academic training with industry needs.

- To encourage practices that support environmental sustainability and resilience in infrastructure projects.

##### FEATURES

- Networking Platform: Provides a platform for civil engineers, contractors, and government bodies to network and collaborate on large-scale projects.

- Knowledge Sharing: Hosts conferences, technical sessions, and seminars for the sharing of knowledge, emerging trends, and technological advancements in the field.

- Certification and Training: Offers specialized certification programs and hands-on training sessions to upskill engineers in new methodologies and technologies.

- Standardization Efforts: Works towards the standardization of civil engineering practices across the region to ensure quality and safety in projects.

- Research and Development: Collaborates with academic institutions to promote research in cutting-edge civil engineering practices.

##### OUTCOMES

- Improved Standards: Enhanced quality and safety standards in civil engineering projects across Tamil Nadu and Pondicherry.

- Professional Growth: A more skilled and qualified civil engineering workforce through continuous learning and professional development opportunities.

- Industry Collaboration: Stronger collaboration between industry, government, and academia leading to more relevant training programs and innovations.

- Sustainable Infrastructure: The adoption of eco-friendly, sustainable building practices resulting in infrastructure projects that are resilient to climate change and natural disasters.

- Policy Influence: Successful advocacy efforts leading to improved regulations and policies that benefit both civil engineers and the community.

##### FUTURE PLAN

- Expansion of Membership: To increase the reach of FACEAT by bringing more civil engineering professionals and associations under its banner from various parts of Tamil Nadu and Pondicherry.

- Digital Transformation: Introduce digital tools and platforms to streamline communication, resource sharing, and project management among members.

- International Collaboration: Establish ties with international civil engineering bodies and organizations to bring global best practices to Tamil Nadu and Pondicherry.

- Green Engineering Initiatives: Promote green engineering initiatives and work with policymakers to encourage sustainable construction practices.

- Mentorship Programs: Launch mentorship programs for young civil engineers to guide them in their professional development and career advancement.

- Policy Advocacy Expansion: Further strengthen advocacy efforts by working closely with regional and national government bodies to influence infrastructure policies that promote innovation, quality, and sustainability.

### ISHRAE

The Indian Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air Conditioning Engineers (ISHRAE), was founded in 1981 at New Delhi by a group of eminent HVAC&R professionals.

##### ISHRAE

The Indian Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air Conditioning Engineers (ISHRAE), was founded in 1981 at New Delhi by a group of eminent HVAC&R professionals. ISHRAE today has more than HVAC&R professionals and Student-members. ISHRAE operates from 44 Chapters and sub-Chapters spread all over India, with HQ in Delhi. It is led by a team of elected officers, who are members of the Society, working on a voluntary basis, and collectively called the Board of Governors.

##### ISHRAE OBJECTIVES

- Advancement of the Arts and Sciences of Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Engineering and Related Services.

- Continuing education of Members and other interested persons in the said sciences through Lectures, Workshops, Product Presentations, Publications and Expositions.

- Rendition of career guidance and financial assistance to students of the said sciences.

- Encouragement of scientific research.

##### AAACET-ISHRAE

AAACET-ISHRAE student professional chapter was inaugurated on 26.10.2018 [Registered SC/2018-19/035]. This chapter is actively contributing to the growth of students in the field of Heating Ventilation and Air Conditioning, by organizing various seminars, industrial visits, technical talk, and workshops. Also this chapter is providing job opportunities for the final year students in the HVAC domain.

text:
### Innovative entrepreneurial idea in building quantity and cost estimation on 12-10-2023

- EDC

- October 28, 2024

The Institution’s Innovation Council (IIC) and Entrepreneurship Development Cell (EDC), in association with the Department of Civil Engineering, organized a Guest Lecture titled ‘Innovative entrepreneurial idea in building quantity and cost estimation.’ The session took place on October 12, 2023, at 03.00 p.m.

Dr. G. Vairamuthu, President of IIC, presided over the event. The session commenced with a welcome address from Mr. M. Sivasankar, EDC Coordinator.

Mr. K. V. Hari Variar, a Consulting Civil Engineer at Sanketha Software Solutions, Kerala, served as the resource person for the session. He initiated the session by explaining the need for estimation software in the civil engineering field. After that, he elaborated on the various parameters that should be considered for developing estimation software. He also shared the difficulties he faced during the marketing of Estima software. Furthermore, he gave a demo of Estima software for the participants. Finally, he motivated the students to create innovative software that addresses the needs of civil engineer.

The session concluded with an interactive question-and-answer segment, during which participants engaged with the speaker.

A total of 43 students participated in the session. The event drew to a close at 04.30 p.m.

We are committed to treat people with at most grace, dignity and promote a strong sense of self worth.

##### Stipulate for Excellence

The excellence of AAACET lies in innovative teaching methodology, novel projects, research in diversified fields and sports activities. We mould our students to be honest, law abiding, responsible and participative citizens of our country. We presume that faculty and students go hand in hand for the progression.

We believe in promoting and nurturing the spirit of knowledge sharing among faculty members. We strive for the prevalence of congenial atmosphere for our faculty members, which foster learning and discovery, and leeway to investigate, apply and transfer knowledge seamlessly.

### E -Yantra

e-Yantra will provide encouragement to the students to come up with new ideas and also to get exposed to the current technologies in the field of Robotics to make them industry ready and increasing their employability.

##### PREAMBLE

AAACET established Centre for eYantra Robotics laboratory in association with IIT Bombay in the year of 2016 with an installation of cost of Rs. 4.5 Lakhs. This laboratory is located at the III rd floor of Cambridge block and it is set up with the Firebird V , Spark V Robots, advanced microcontrollers, sensors & actuators, interfacing devices and network Interfaces.

##### The major objectives of the e-Yantra Center are:

- To Provide knowledge on the basic concepts of embedded systems and Robotics.

- To create the next generation of embedded systems engineers with a practical outlook to help provide practical solutions to some of the real-world problems.

- To encourage the students to participate in various Robotic competitions at national and international level confidently.

- Enhance the problem-solving skills with an integrated approach while working on multi-disciplinary engineering projects like Robotics.

- Organize various events like special lectures, seminars, workshops and certification courses for enhancing the students’ knowledge on embedded systems and robotics.

##### OUTCOMES:

After successful completion of the course, the students are able to

- Identify the basic components and sensors for designing various type of robots based on the requirements.

- Interface various types of sensors and modules with firebird V and Spark V robots.

- Analyze various communication protocols and modules used in robots

- Design robots using advanced microcontrollers and embedded systems

- Design robots for home automation and IOT based applications.

##### Admissions through Management Quota

For admission to AAA College of Engineering and Technology under Management Quota, each candidate should apply to the Association of Self Financing Colleges who will rank the students based on the qualifying examination and rank order will be published by the Association. Based on the ranking by the Association the candidate will be selected. The above procedure will be taken care of by the college.

The students who are willing to join under management quota are requested to visit the college and get details about the courses and fees structure etc.

##### Admissions through Government Quota

TNEA (Tamil Nadu Engineering Admission ) is a state level counselling for admission to the undergraduate B.E/ B.Tech degree courses offered by the institutions or colleges located in the limits of Tamil Nadu state. TNEA counselling form will be issued for the students who completed higher secondary on every year. Tamilnadu Engineering Admission TNEA is an authority conducting counselling for the 12th students who wants join in B.E, B.Tech, B.Arch. And students from other states can also pursue engineering education from TNEA admission process. Everyone should apply online before the last date

##### TNEA B.E./B.Tech. Eligibility

The candidates should be the native of Tamil Nadu state are eligible to apply. The outside candidates studied their schooling in Tamil Nadu may also apply. The children of persons who have been serving in Public sector or government sector for the last five years in Tamil Nadu may also apply for TNEA. The candidates must have passed the 12th (intermediate) or its equivalent examination from the government recognized board with the subjects as Physics, Mathematics and Chemistry with the percentage as 45% (for general candidates), 40% (for backward class including Muslim), 40% (MBC & DNC) and 40% (for SC/ST/SCA) candidates.

B.E/B.TECH INFORMATION BROCHURE

##### TNEA M.E./M.Tech Eligibility

To be eligible for a TNEA M.E./M.Tech program, you must have a bachelor’s degree (B.E./B.Tech.) in a relevant engineering discipline, or a relevant B.Sc. or M.Sc. degree, depending on the specific specialization. A minimum percentage of marks (often around 50-55%) is required, with relaxations for reserved categories. Admission is primarily through the Tamil Nadu Common Entrance Test (TANCET), and you must have passed the qualifying degree without distance or weekend learning for your B.E./B.Tech.

##### TNEA PhD Eligibility

To be eligible for a PhD at Anna University, you need a Master’s degree with at least 55% marks (or a CGPA of 5.5 on a 10-point scale). For SC/ST/Differently-abled candidates, the minimum requirement is 50% marks (or a CGPA of 5.0 on a 10-point scale).

The Reverse Osmosis Plant installed in the college campus caters to the drinking water needs of all the students, faculty, supporting staff and the visitors. The raw water with an average Total Dissolved Solids [TDS] of 750-1000 ppm is treated to reduce the TDS content to less than 100 ppm the generally acceptable upper limit of the TDS. This is done in three stages, namely: Pre treatment, passage of the water through 12 RO membrane filters held in parallel to each other {main process] and Post treatment. The maximum capacity of the plant is 2500-3000 lit/hr and the utilized capacity is 1000 lit/hr. This water is pure, tasty and hygienic rendering it highly suitable for human consumption.

This plant not only facilitates the supply of safe drinking water but also obviates the otherwise involved huge expenditure for procuring drinking water for the large number of people in the campus. ###### Comprehensive Electrical Infrastructure and Power Backup

The AAA COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING & TECHNOLOGY maintains a secure and highly reliable electrical infrastructure, crucial for sustaining its advanced academic environment. The campus’s primary power is distributed through a 200 KVA High Tension (H.T.) Line , while power quality is rigorously managed by a massive 500 KVA H.T. EB Transformer and a high-performance 250 KVA, 3-Phase KRYKARD Stabilizer . This industry-leading stabilizer actively and precisely regulates voltage fluctuations , thereby safeguarding all sensitive laboratory equipment, sophisticated IT systems, and critical assets from damage.

To ensure absolute continuity, the college relies on a robust, multi-tiered power backup system :

- The high-capacity 380 KVA KOEL Green Generator serves as the primary backup source for the entire college, keeping all main infrastructure operational during grid outages.

- A 125 KVA KOEL Green Generator is dedicated exclusively to the college’s overall lighting load , ensuring campus-wide illumination.

- A 35 KVA Kirloskar Green Generator is installed to cater solely to the Girls’ Hostel , operating as a dedicated, automatic generator system for seamless power transition.

This layered approach guarantees uninterrupted, stable 24/7 power for all academic, IT, research, and residential activities.

### FDP on Internet of Things

- January 27, 2019

Two days faculty development program on Internet of Things in association with Riyassa Labs was held on 16-01-2019 and 17-01-2019 at Centre for IIoT, AAA College of Engineering and Technology. This FDP made the participants to realize the importance of IoT and its applications in various fields. This training was imparted in different applications of wireless, embedded and IoT using lecture sessions, hands on training and developing product ideas into a working prototype.

Day wise report as follows:

Day 1: Session I – 16.01.2019

The course started with a formal inauguration ceremony. Experts from Riyassa Labs delivered the origin and importance of IoT followed by the recent development of IoT. He gave talk on basics of sensors and actuators, Arduino programming – Interfacing and configuration of sensors with arduino software.

Day 1: Session II – 16.01.2019

Experts handled hands on training on working with sensors like Temperature, Humidity, IR Sensor, Ultrasonic Sensor, Gas Sensor, Light and Moisture Sensor, PIR and Color Sensors.

Day 2: Session I – 17.01.2019

The faculty members worked with HC-05 Bluetooth module by controlling the sensors and actuators using HC-05 module Bluetooth mobile app. By using this concept, faculty members designed a smart home system of controlling the light and fan using mobile app.

Day 2: Session II – 17.01.2019

This session had an expert talk about the Node MCU – ESP8266 and integrating the sensor real time values to the cloud. The sensed data is uploaded to the ThingsSpeak cloud using ESP8266 Module. The real time data is visualized as graphical representation using matlab code available in the cloud. The session was followed by the closing ceremony.

Outcomes of the FDP program

- Participants would be familiar with IoT systems and applications.

- Participants would be able to work with various sensors and actuators.

- Participants would be able to design an IoT – smart system using Bluetooth module and ESP8266.

- Participants would be able to integrate sensors with cloud and access real time data.

#### About College

AAA College of Engineering and Technology, Sivakasi was established in the year 2013, is one among the renowned colleges for imparting technical education in the fireworks city. It is branded for its quality education, through Panjurajan Amaravathy trust, Thiruthangal, Virudhunagar District and Promoted by Vinayaga Sony fireworks group of industries. The trust also manages two schools namely, Glory Matriculation Higher Secondary School and AAA International School (CBSE) in Thiruthangal. There by providing quality education right from schooling itself.

AAA College of Engineering and Technology located in the district of Virudhunagar is the one of the youngest institutions accredited with NAAC ‘A’ grade and TUV-ISO 21001: 2018 certification in Tamilnadu. The institution is focused on carrying out research in diversified fields of engineering and was recently granted with the recognition for Ph.D. programme in Mechanical Department by the centre for research, Anna University Research centre. The faculty of AAACET has produced more than 400 papers published in high reputed journals.

#### About Conference

AAACET invites you to participate in the INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON ENVIRONMENTAL DEVELOPMENT USING COMPUTER SCIENCE (ICECS’ 2024) , which will be held at AAA College of Engineering and Technology in Sivakasi, Tamil Nadu. ICECS’ 2024 offers a great platform to showcase impactful ideas on energy and environmental conservation. Through data analytics, computer science contributes to sustainable engineering by collecting and analyzing data on energy consumption, emissions, and other environmental factors. Engineers can identify opportunities for improvement and optimize their designs for maximum sustainability.

With data analytics, renewable energy development, transportation optimization, and waste reduction, computer science has the potential to revolutionize sustainable engineering and make our world a more sustainable place. To achieve this, the conference brings together experts from academia and industry to develop innovative ideas that address society’s environmental sustainability needs.”

Separate Hostels for Boys and Girls are functioning in the premises of AAA College of Engineering and Technology, Sivakasi. Hostels are located in an environment which is safe and good for learning. ##### Major Functions by Exam Cell

- The college has an Examination Cell for overseeing the conduct of all the internal and University end semester examinations. The Examination cell consists of Principal (Chief COE), COE, Exam cell Coordinator, Assistant Exam cell members and clerks.

- Enrolling the students for the regular courses, professional electives and open electives for every semester in the Anna University COE Web portal.

- Conducting Internal Assessment Examinations (Theory) as per time slots provided by the Anna University.

- Conducting the University end semester Practical and Theory exam as per the time table provided by the Anna University.

- Registering the students for the end semester practical and theory exams, payment of exam fees collected from the students to the Anna University, issuing the hall ticket, grade sheet, etc.,

- Arranging for photo-copy/re-evaluation of University end semester answer-booklets as requested by the students upon payment of necessary fees as prescribed by Anna University.

- The Exam Cell shall ensure proper organization, execution and coordinate all types of examinations (TNPSC, TRB, etc.).

- The Exam Cell shall maintain all the students’ academic performance records and any other documents related to examinations safe and confidentially.

##### Internal Exam Process

- Internal Examinations are conducted based on the Academic Schedule prescribed by the Anna University and one model exam for theory subjects is conducted before the start of their University examinations to make them well prepared for their University examinations.

- The Internal Examination Timetable will be released 2 weeks before commencement of examinations.

- Once the examinations are conducted, the answer scripts of students are evaluated and verified by the HOD to ensure that there is no discrepancy or partiality in the valuation.

- Conducting the University end semester Practical and Theory exam as per the time table provided by the Anna University.

- At the end of every semester external audit by a senior faculty member from other department is done to ensure the quality of evaluation.

- Arranging for photo-copy/re-evaluation of University end semester answer-booklets as requested by the students upon payment of necessary fees as prescribed by Anna University.

- The answer scripts are distributed to the students by the faculty members within two days of examination.

- The Exam Cell shall maintain all the students’ academic performance records and any other documents related to examinations safe and confidentially.

- The faculty members discuss the answers to all the questions given in the examinations during the distribution of answer scripts to the students. This helps the students to understand their mistakes and note down the corrections.

- Special Coaching and improvement Test is conducted for the slow learners in the subsequently once all the examinations are over.

### ICREGD- 2025

International Conference on Renewable Energy Generation and Distribution (ICREGD 2025) February 07th & 08th, 2025 at AAA College of Engineering & Technology, Kamarajar Educational Road, Amathur – 626 005.

#### About College

AAA College of Engineering and Technology located in the district of Virudhunagar is the one of the youngest institutions accredited with NAAC ‘A’ grade and TUV-ISO 21001: 2018 certification in Tamilnadu. The institution is focused on carrying out research in diversified fields of engineering and was recently granted with the recognition for Ph.D. programme in Mechanical Department by the centre for research, Anna University Research centre. The faculty of AAACET has produced more than 400 papers published in high reputed journals.

#### About Conference

International Conference on Renewable Energy Generation and Distribution (ICREGD 2025) February 07th & 08th, 2025 at AAA College of Engineering & Technology, Kamarajar Educational Road, Amathur – 626 005.

The International Conference on Renewable Energy Generation and Distribution (ICREGD 2025) will bring together leading experts, researchers, and industry professionals to explore the transformative impact of renewable energy technologies on the future of power generation and distribution. This conference will provide a platform to discuss the latest advancements in renewable energy, including solar, wind, hydropower, and biomass, and examine the innovative strategies needed to integrate these energy sources into the power grid.

ICREGD 2025 will emphasize key areas such as energy storage technologies, including advancements in battery systems, supercapacitors, and hybrid energy storage solutions that address the intermittency of renewable power generation. The event will also cover cutting-edge developments in power electronics, with a focus on multilevel inverters, Flexible AC Transmission Systems (FACTS), and smart grid innovations that enhance the reliability and efficiency of renewable energy distribution.

The conference will also delve into the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) in renewable energy, showcasing their use in predictive modeling for resource forecasting, AI-driven optimization of energy systems, and intelligent control mechanisms for enhancing system performance. Discussions will also include distributed energy resources (DERs) and the growing importance of microgrids, with a particular focus on integrating renewable energy into decentralized power systems to improve energy resilience.

In addition to technological innovations, ICREGD 2025 will cover the critical policy and economic factors influencing renewable energy projects. This includes an exploration of financial strategies, government policies, and incentives aimed at promoting green technology adoption, as well as discussions on sustainable business models that can support large-scale renewable energy deployment.

The environmental impact of renewable energy will also be a significant theme, with topics including life cycle analysis, strategies for reducing the carbon footprint of energy systems, and the broader environmental benefits of transitioning to renewable energy sources.

Through these discussions, ICREGD 2025 aims to foster collaboration among researchers, engineers, policymakers, and industry leaders, promoting the exchange of innovative ideas and strategies for advancing the use of renewable energy in power generation and distribution. This event will contribute to the development of sustainable, resilient, and efficient energy systems that will shape the future of global energy infrastructure.

ICREGD 2025 has a set of policies that all authors are required to follow. These policies are categorized as follows:

Submission Policy: Only original research papers will be considered for review. Review papers and short notes are not eligible for submission. All papers must comply with the prescribed format of the conference, and those that do not adhere to the guidelines will be rejected without entering the review process. Authors must follow the submission timeline of ICREGD 2025, and multiple submissions are strictly prohibited. Authors are invited to submit research that has not been published or submitted elsewhere.

Withdrawal Policy: Authors can withdraw their papers at any time under certain conditions. Withdrawal can be done easily through the CMT system during the review process. Papers may also be withdrawn after acceptance. Refunds will follow the timeline below:

Full Refund: Papers withdrawn on or before 20th November 2024 will receive a full refund of the registration fee, after applicable tax deductions.

50% Refund: Papers withdrawn between 21st November and 30th November 2024 will be eligible for a 50% refund.

25% Refund: Papers withdrawn between 1st December and 4th December 2024 will receive a 25% refund. No withdrawals or refunds will be accepted after these dates.

Plagiarism Policy: ICREGD 2025 enforces a strict anti-plagiarism policy. After excluding references and author biographies, plagiarism checks will be conducted. Only papers with less than 20% plagiarism will proceed to review. Papers with plagiarism between 21% and 30% will be returned to authors for revisions. Papers with more than 31% plagiarism will be rejected without review.

Review Policy: Once a paper passes the plagiarism check, it will undergo a single-blind review by at least two independent reviewers. All reviews will be conducted through the CMT system. Reviewers are required to submit their reports within the specified timeline. The Technical Program Committee (TPC) will oversee the process. Reviewers will receive a certificate of honor (soft copy). To qualify as a reviewer, candidates must be research scholars or PhD holders affiliated with reputable institutions. Interested reviewers can send an email request and must have an account in the Microsoft CMT System.

Acceptance Policy: Papers will be accepted based on quality, novelty, research objectives, language, presentation, validation, results, analysis, and appropriate references. A letter of acceptance will be sent via the CMT system. Authors may be required to make minor revisions before final acceptance. Authors will be notified immediately if their paper is rejected.

Registration Policy: At least one author of an accepted paper must register for ICREGD 2025 to include the paper in the conference schedule for presentation and proceedings. The registration fee covers the conference kit, presentation, certificate, and proceedings. Registration fees vary by session. More details will be provided in the acceptance letter, along with payment instructions.

Presentation Policy: All authors of accepted papers must present their papers during a 15-minute PowerPoint presentation, conducted exclusively offline. However, under special circumstances, ICREGD 2025 may allow a limited number of papers to be presented online, subject to prior approval. Each presentation will be strictly timed to 15 minutes, with 12 minutes for the presentation and 3 minutes for questions and feedback.

Certificate Policy: All conference participants will receive a printed participation certificate. Authors who present their papers will receive a presentation certificate. Final Version Submission Policy: All authors of accepted papers must submit their final versions within 5 days after the conference, following the publication format specified for each session.

Publication Policy: High-quality papers presented at ICREGD 2025 will be submitted to the respective publication partners for potential publication. ###### RAGGING IS STRICTLY PROHIBITED INSIDE THE COLLEGE CAMPUS

As per the UGC/AICTE regulations on curbing the menace of ragging in higher educational institutions (2009), the establishment of an Anti-Ragging Cell is carried out in our institution to uphold a ragging-free culture on campus.

The committee’s primary objectives include raising awareness among students about the harmful effects of ragging, maintaining constant vigilance to prevent its occurrence, and taking immediate and strict action against any reported incidents. Students can approach any member of the committee in person or call them to report any action of ragging inside / outside the campus. The committee is aided by the college anti-ragging squad which constantly keep its vigilance.

In line with the Supreme Court’s directives, ragging is defined as any intentional act by a student or group of students that includes indiscipline, teasing, rude behaviour, or any action that disrupts academic activities. It also includes actions causing annoyance, hardship, psychological harm, or fear; financial extortion or forceful spending; physical abuse or harm; verbal abuse or public insult through spoken words, emails, or messages; infringement of human dignity; wrongful confinement; molestation; criminal acts; and conspiracy or unlawful assembly aimed at ragging.

Students found guilty of ragging, whether on or off-campus, will face strict disciplinary action which may lead to cancellation of admission.

#### Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering (Ph.D. Admission Open for Full Time/Part Time)

The Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering has been recognized as a Research Centre by Centre for Research, Anna University, Chennai.

The department offers research opportunities in Smart Grid Technologies, Renewable Energy Systems, Industrial IoT, Power Electronics, Electric Vehicles, Embedded Systems, Automation, and Intelligent Control Systems with modern laboratories, various Centre of Excellences, infrastructure and industry collaboration support, to draft proposals about industrial and societal based challenges to the various government funding agencies.

### Fresher’s Day

- September 15, 2019

The Fresher’s Party held on 10 th September 2019 was marked as a memorable day in the life of every fresher at AAA College of Engineering and Technology. The fresher’s day was a day that was filled with excitement, joy, music, enthusiasm, laughter and happiness. The celebration started at 2 p.m. And the cool seniors put up various performances like dancing, singing and skits to entertain their juniors, all the juniors were enjoying and having a great time. This year the department had planned the fresher’s party for the newly admitted budding engineers (2019-2023) in a very unique and special way.

### Future India

- September 9, 2017

AAA College of Engineering &Technology organized a special MOTIVATIONAL program called “Future India” on 9th September 2017 around 11 a.m. in the college A/C seminar hall. Shree R.RANGARAJ PANDEY, Chief News Editor, Thanthi Tv was the guest of honor of the program.Correspondent Dr. P.Ganesan welcomed the gathering. The chief guest, Shree Rangaraj Pandey, in his speech, advised the students about the present scenario of what’s going on around the world and they should take all their failures as a motivational force to attain their goals. He also insisted the students to have a very good knowledge of their domain and upgrade themselves in recent technology to excel in life. “Students should develop their entrepreneurial skills”, he added. He wished that one of our AAA College of Engineering and Technology students should become a business tycoon. Followed by this there was a questionnaire session. Our students asked number of questions and the Chief Guest Shree Pandey also replied to those questions with all ease. He was very much pleased by the active participation of the students. Towards the end he advised the students to concentrate on their studies and to establish themselves in life. Then they should shoulder the social responsibilities.

### ICRICCM 2023

ICRICCM 2023 is a forum for presenting excellent results and new challenges facing the field of Computer Science, Communication and Manufacturing and all other technologies.

#### About College

AAA College of Engineering and Technology located in the district of Virudhunagar is the one of the youngest institutions accredited with NAAC ‘A’ grade and TUV-ISO 21001: 2018 certification in Tamilnadu. The institution is focused on carrying out research in diversified fields of engineering and was recently granted with the recognition for PhD programme in Mechanical Department by the centre for research, Anna University Research centre. The faculty of AAACET has produced more than 400 papers published in high reputed journals.

#### About Conference

AAACET is happy to invite you all to contribute and participate in the First International Conference on Computer, Communication and Manufacturing (ICRICCM 2023) , which will be held in AAA College of Engineering and Technology, Sivakasi, Tamilnadu, India during April 12 th & 13 th , 2023. ICRICCM 2023 is a forum for presenting excellent results and new challenges facing the field of Computer Science, Communication and Manufacturing and all other technologies.

It brings together specialists from business, government, and academia with backgrounds in engineering, design, and research. Three seminars on Computer Technology, Electronics and Materials will also be held.

### Centre of IIoT

The centre of IIoT is to impart knowledge in Internet of Things to all our students and to train them with the requirement of the nation to become technocrats as well as entrepreneurs

#### Centre of IIoT

AAACET established Centre for Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) laboratory in association with Riyasaa labs in the year of 2018 with an installation of cost of Rs. 9 Lakhs. This laboratory is located at the II floor (Room No: 2233) of Cambridge block and it is set up with the higher end computers, advanced embedded controllers, sensors & actuators, interfacing devices and network Interfaces.

#### OBJECTIVE

The main objective of this Centre of Excellence is to enhance and enrich the students’ knowledge in Internet of Things and to train them to become technocrats as well as entrepreneurs in IoT technology.

#### Features

- Students gain valuable and marketable Hands-on learning experience through certificate courses and workshop.

- Students are permitted to utilize this laboratory to transform their innovative idea into working model.

- Renowned experts from Industry and Academia are being invited to share their view on emerging trends in IoT and hence the students can have opportunity to interact with industry experts to sharpen the knowledge.

- Student can utilize this centre in the view of participating in the National level contest such as, Smart India Hackathon (SIH), E-Yantra Robotics Competition National Innovation Contest (NIC) and can get guidance from the trainers.

#### About College

Established in 2013 in Sivakasi, Tamil Nadu, AAA College of Engineering and Technology (AAACET) is a premier Institution for quality technical education in the region. Approved by AICTE and affiliated with Anna University, AAACET upholds the highest standards of academic governance while nurturing curiosity, innovation, and excellence.

The college’s NBA accreditation for five engineering programmes reflects its consistent commitment to outcome-based education and its focus on preparing industry-ready graduates with globally relevant skills.

Our vision is to be a center of excellence in engineering education — driving innovation, research, and technological advancement while shaping ethically grounded professionals who contribute meaningfully to society. To achieve this, AAACET is committed to delivering outcome-based education through modern infrastructure and experienced faculty; fostering a culture of innovation, research, and lifelong learning; bridging academia and industry through internships and collaborations; instilling ethical values and professional integrity; and empowering students to become responsible citizens and future leaders.

AAACET’s vibrant campus features state-of-the-art infrastructure and advanced laboratories that mirror real-world industry settings. Guided by experienced faculty, students gain a strong blend of theoretical knowledge and hands-on learning — graduating with genuine, applicable competence.

The institution actively nurtures innovation and research through internships, technical symposiums, conferences, seminars, and workshops — giving students a real edge in their professional journeys.

Beyond technical skills, AAACET is committed to strong ethical values and social responsibility. Its holistic approach extends beyond academics into community engagement, shaping graduates who are skilled, principled, and civic-minded. Together, this integrated approach — combining academic rigor, industry exposure and ethical grounding — enables AAACET to nurture responsible citizens, dynamic leaders and socially committed professionals dedicated to national progress.

#### About the department

The Department of Science and Humanities serves as the cornerstone of engineering education, providing students with a strong foundation in Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, and English. The department is dedicated to nurturing analytical thinking, scientific temperament, communication competence and professional ethics that are essential for success in engineering and technology.

With a team of highly qualified faculty members, modern laboratories, language learning facilities, and an outcome-based learning approach, the department creates an academic environment that encourages innovation, critical thinking, and lifelong learning. Mathematics strengthens logical reasoning and problem-solving abilities, while Physics enables students to understand the fundamental principles governing the physical world. Chemistry equips learners with knowledge of materials, industrial processes, and environmental sustainability, and English enhances communication, interpersonal, and professional skills required in the global workplace. The department emphasizes experiential learning through laboratory experiments, interactive teaching methods, skill-development activities, and technology-enabled education. By integrating scientific knowledge with human values, the Department of Science and Humanities prepares students to meet the challenges of higher studies, research, industry, and society with confidence and competence.

Committed to academic excellence and holistic development, the department plays a vital role in shaping responsible engineers, innovative thinkers, and future leaders capable of contributing to sustainable technological advancement and societal progress.

The conference aims to foster interdisciplinary collaboration, promote cuttingedge research, and address contemporary challenges through the integration of science, technology, humanities, artificial intelligence, and sustainable digital practices. It provides a vibrant platform for the exchange of innovative ideas, research findings, and best practices that contribute to societal progress and global sustainability. Through keynote lectures, technical sessions, panel discussions, and research presentations, NextGen–2026 encourages meaningful dialogue between academia and industry, inspiring solutions that are innovative, inclusive, and future-focused. The conference seeks to advance knowledge, strengthen global partnerships, and empower participants to shape a smarter, sustainable, and digitally transformed world.

Graduates will apply the fundamentals of mathematics, computer science and engineering knowledge to understand, analyze and develop computer programs in the areas related to database, operating system, data structures, algorithms and networking for efficient design of computer-based systems of varying complexity.

Graduates will apply the domain knowledge to provide optimized solutions by research and innovations in emerging fields of computer science and engineering leading to successful professional careers.

### Program Educational Objectives (PEOs)

Graduates will become competent Computer Professionals by applying the knowledge of advanced computer concepts and recent tools to develop software in emerging technologies for the betterment of industries and society.

Graduates will have a successful career in Academics/ Research by enhancing their technical & communication skills through sustained learning.

Graduates will become Entrepreneurs / Software Consultants in the multi-disciplinary environment by having comprehensive experience and self-confidence.

### PROGRAM OUTCOMES

PO-1 | Engineering knowledge : Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems.
PO-2 | Problem analysis : Identify, formulate, research literature, and analyze engineering problems to arrive at substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural, and engineering sciences.
PO-3 | Design/development of solutions : Design solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components, processes to meet the specifications with consideration for the public health and safety, and the cultural, societal, and environmental considerations.
PO-4 | Conduct investigations of complex problems : Use research-based knowledge including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of the information to provide valid conclusions.
PO-5 | Modern tool usage : Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools including prediction and modeling to complex engineering activities with an understanding of the limitations.
PO-6 | The engineer and society : Apply reasoning informed by the contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal, and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to the professional engineering practice.
PO-7 | Environment and sustainability : Understand the impact of the professional engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts, and demonstrate the knowledge of, and need for sustainable development.
PO-8 | Ethics : Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities and norms of the engineering practice.
PO-9 | Individual and team work : Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in teams, and in multidisciplinary settings.
PO-10 | Communication : Communicate effectively with the engineering community and with society at large. Be able to comprehend and write effective reports documentation. Make effective presentations, and give and receive clear instructions.
PO-11 | Project management and finance : Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of engineering and management principles and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team. Manage projects in multidisciplinary environments.
PO-12 | Life-long learning : Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change.

###### Double-Blind Peer Review

- To ensure impartiality and maintain the highest standards of quality, ICMIST-24 employs a double-blind peer review process. This means that both the reviewers and authors remain anonymous throughout the review process.

###### Detailed Review Process

Submission:

- Authors submit their manuscripts through the conference submission system, ensuring that no identifying information is included in the manuscript itself to maintain anonymity.

Initial Check:

- The conference organizers conduct an initial check to ensure that the submission adheres to the conference’s formatting and submission guidelines.

- Submissions that do not comply with the guidelines may be returned to authors for correction before being sent for review.

Plagiarism Check:

- All submissions undergo a plagiarism check to ensure originality. The acceptable plagiarism rate is between 10-15%. Manuscripts exceeding this threshold will be returned to authors for revision or rejected.

Assignment to Reviewers:

- Manuscripts passing the initial check and plagiarism screening are assigned to at least two independent reviewers with expertise in the relevant field.

Review Phase:

- Reviewers evaluate the manuscript based on its originality, technical quality, relevance to the conference topics, clarity of presentation, and significance of the research.

- Reviewers provide detailed feedback and recommendations for acceptance, minor revisions, major revisions, or rejection.

Decision:

- Based on the reviewers’ feedback, the conference program committee makes a decision on each manuscript.

- Decisions can be one of the following: Accept, Accept with Minor Revisions, Accept with Major Revisions, or Reject.

Notification:

- Authors are notified of the decision along with the reviewers’ comments and recommendations. If revisions are required, authors are given a deadline to resubmit their revised manuscript.

Final Acceptance:

- Revised manuscripts are reviewed again (if necessary) to ensure all reviewer comments have been addressed satisfactorily.

- The final decision on acceptance is made, and authors are notified.

Publication:

- Accepted papers are included in the conference proceedings and scheduled for presentation during the conference.

Transparency and Availability

- Detailed information about the review process is available on the ICMIST-24 website. Authors are encouraged to review this information prior to submission to ensure understanding of the review procedures and expectations.

###### Guidelines for Authors

- Same authors submit not more than 2 Research articles.

- Papers are good quality and original research articles.

However, we strongly recommend that you write concisely and stick to the following guidelines:

- Articles should ideally be no more than 10 typeset pages.

- The main text should be no more than 4,500 words.

- The title should be no more than 20 words.

- The abstract should be no more than 200 words.

- References not more than 20, self-citations maximum 4.

EDITOR(S)

Bui Thanh Hung , Data Science Department, Faculty of Information Technology, Industrial University, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. He has published 35 research articles scopus indexed books and 30 book chapters 46 international conference, 21 national conference, 123 journals reviewers for special issue. He delivered 47 Invited tals, organizing 2 international conferences.

M. Sekar , a well-known academician has taken charge as Principal of AAA college of Engineering and Technology, Sivakasi, Tamilnadu, India since July 2018. He brings his wide and rich administrative, industrial, research and international exposure to achieve the vision and build institutions.

Ayhan ESİ is currently working as a Professor in Malatya Turgut Ozal University, Yeşilyurt, Malatya, Turkey. His research interests include Summability Theory, Sequences and Series in Analysis and Functional Analysis.

R. Senthil Kumar is an Associate Professor in Science and Humanities, AAA College of Engineering and Technology, Sivakasi, Tamilnadu, India. His areas of interest are Mathematics, Network Theory, Enterprise Resource Planning, Analytics, Information Technology and Statistical Packages.

### Annual Day 2017

AAA College of Engineering & Technology, celebrated its 4th Annual Day on 1st of April 2017, in a grand manner at The Open Air theatre of AAA Campus. Shri. M. RAJA RAJAN SUPERINTENDENT OF POLICE (Virudhunagar district) was the chief guest for the occasion.

The programme started with a prayer song. Dr. P. GANESAN, Correspondent, AAA College of Engineering & Technology, extended a warm welcome to the gathering by giving a welcome address. Shri. P. PANJURAJAN, Chairman, & Dr. P. KARVANNAN, Secretary presided over the function. Dr. ARULMOZHI, Principal, AAA College presented the Annual Report of the College for the academic year 2015-2016.

Finally, there was a cultural programme. In the colourful show, students brought to limelight their creative and artistic talents. Mrs.Gladima Nisha, Assistant Professor proposed a vote of thanks.

### ECO NATURE CLUB

The Eco Nature Club aims to inculcate the global challenges locally and environmentally in terms of climate change, pollution and resource depletion.

### About Eco Nature Club

The Eco Nature Club aims to inculcate the global challenges locally and environmentally in terms of climate change, pollution and resource depletion. The Club nurtures amongst the students to have Eco tours to promote green practices such as sustainable building designs, green spaces and eco – friendly campus policies. Also it provides leadership opportunities for students to take initiative on environmental projects and raise awareness within the student body. The club scrutinizes to have a gentle rapport with other bodies like district administration, forestry and NGO’s

### Objectives

- To educate the students about the environment

- To create a clean and green consciousness amongst the students through various activities

- To involve them in various activities to reach the eco and society based organizations

- To imbibe the gentle qualities such as minimum waste generation and true lovers of nature

### Vision

Imply the ideology among the students and faculty to practise the behavior in maintaining the campus green and clean with healthy and well protected environment

### Mission

- To have the niche between human and nature

- To Practise the vitality of green and clean campus and to protect the environment user – friendly

- To impart the importance of environment amongst the students

- To have the niche between human and nature

- To Practise the vitality of green and clean campus and to protect the environment user – friendly

### Outcomes

- Administer the knowledge of general ecological knowledge and to find solutions for some ecological problems

- Imbibe the ethics in life involving the activities and evolving as a noble human being

- Imitate the issues and find solutions for environmental issues or conflicts

- Apply the contextual knowledge into society – based outputs

text:
### AAACET is organizing Graduation Day on 26-07-2026

- July 27, 2026

The 9th Graduation Day of AAA College of Engineering and Technology, Sivakasi, was celebrated with great enthusiasm on 26 July 2026 at the college campus.

The ceremony was graced by Dr. P. Karvannan, Secretary & Chairman Dr. P. Correspondent, and Mr. Abishek Pandian, Trustee, who presided over the function. Dr. M. Sekar, Principal, AAACET, chaired the event. The Chief Guest, Dr. M. Kanthababu, Director, Centre for Research, Anna University, Chennai, conferred the degrees upon the graduating students and delivered the graduation address.

The programme commenced with the welcome address delivered by Dr. S.Krishnapriya, Head of the Department of Civil Engineering. This was followed by the presentation of the Graduation Day Report by the Principal, Dr. M. Sekar. In his report, he highlighted the institution’s commitment to providing quality education, state-of-the-art laboratory facilities, research infrastructure, industry collaborations, placement training initiatives, and the remarkable campus placement achievements of the students.

In his presidential address, Dr. P. Ganesan, Correspondent stated that Graduation Day is not only a milestone for the students but also a day of recognition for the dedication, sacrifices, and encouragement of their parents. He further emphasized that AAACET continues to motivate students by providing scholarships, incentives, and merit awards to support their academic excellence.

During his Special address, Dr. M. Kanthababu remarked that Graduation Day marks not merely the completion of academic education but also the beginning of a new journey filled with opportunities and achievements. He urged the graduates to remain grateful to their parents and teachers throughout their lives. He also advised them to associate with positive-minded individuals and ignore negativity. Furthermore, he encouraged the students to continuously enhance their knowledge in emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Cyber Security, Machine Learning, and Electric Vehicles (EVs). He stressed the importance of research, innovation, and entrepreneurial thinking in building a distinctive professional identity and achieving success in their careers. As part of the celebration, faculty members of the college who had completed their Doctoral Degrees (Ph.D.) during the previous year were honoured with certificates of appreciation. In addition, Ms. S. Selvapriya, a graduate of the Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering, was felicitated with a Certificate of Appreciation and a Memento for securing State level First Rank in the Anna University Ranking List, bringing laurels to the institution. Subsequently, around 200 students from various departments of the 2021-2025 batch received their degree certificates from the Chief Guest, Dr. Kanthababu. The programme concluded with the vote of thanks delivered by Dr. C. Senthil Kumar, Professor & Head of the Department of EEE.

### SPRECHEN WITH HR

- August 9, 2018

AAA College of Engineering and Technology, Sivakasi organized a one day workshop on “Preparing and Planning for a Career” for the final year students on 04/08/2018. The workshop started with our traditional touch of Lamp lighting. Dr.R.Sivasangari, Director/Vocational Courses welcomed the gathering. Dr.M.Sekar, Principal, AAA College of Engineering and Technology, Sivakasi gave the felicitation address and motivated the minds of young budding engineers by sharing his vast experience and all-embracing knowledge. Er.K.Vignesh Kumar /Joint Secretary, AAA College of Engineering and technology, Sivakasi honored the chief guest with the memento and delivered the presidential address on the grand occasion and encouraged all the participants to have a successful career life. The Chief Guest from a reputed MNC addressed our final year students on Interview techniques, positive perception, career mapping and Job perspective & Life. He conducted the activity based training for the students, through that they were able to identify their strength & weakness. Further they were capable of analyzing the opportunities and threats behind them. Students found this one day “Sprechen with HR” very useful and informative.

#### Advanced Data Structures and Algorithms Laboratory

December 5, 2025

### Industrial Visits

The purpose of these visits is to bridge the gap between theoretical learning and practical implementation, giving students a well-rounded perspective on their chosen field.

#### INDUSTRIAL VISITS

Industrial visit has its own importance in a career of a student who is pursuing a professional degree as the classroom is not sufficient to provide student an insight to internal working of companies. Industrial visit is considered as one of the tactical methods of teaching. The main reason behind this- Industrial visit helps to combine theoretical knowledge with industrial knowledge and gives them exposure to current work practices. It lets student to know things practically through interaction, working methods and employment practices.

Industrial visits are arranged by our college to students with an objective of providing students functional opportunity in different sectors like IT, Manufacturing and services, finance and marketing as students will be more concerned about earning a job after having an industrial visit.

#### TECHNICAL TRAINING

AAA offers a number of value added courses beyond curriculum that equips students for a successful career. Faculty Development Programs are conducted to our faculties to enhance their knowledge in their expertise field and to keep them updated about the technological advancements in the field. Our faculties combine professional and industrial experience with the latest approaches in learning and teaching.

- Students of Civil Engineering Department are given intensive training in AutoCAD, REVIT architecture, STADD Pro and ANSYS.

- The Department of Computer Science and Engineering conducts training in C, Java, Database MySQL , PHP, AWS, IOT and SalesForce ADX 201.

- The Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering offers extensive training in PSPICE circuit simulation software, MATLAB programming, VLSI Design and Embedded Systems.

- The Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering conducts hands on training in PSPICE circuit simulation, MATLAB programming, Power World Simulator, IOT, E-CAD and LABVIEW.

- Mechanical Department students are made to work in CAD/CAM, CreO, SPRUTCAM, ANSYS, 3D Printing and BOSCH Diagnostic Lab.

#### VALUE ADDED COURSES

The value added courses comprise of a wide range of short courses and workshops that are carefully planned to meet the interests of students, as well as help diversify their skills and technical knowledge. These courses have been selected after analyzing the work profiles and career portrayals of various job roles in core industries and IT companies. These programs will run parallel to the conventional degrees. At the end of year, the students will be equipped with Certificates in value added courses along with a conventional degree.

Value added courses are designed and offered by all the departments for the benefit of the students. Our Faculty members were well trained and certified by authorized certification organizations. From their expertise, our students gain knowledge, which will qualify them to face the formidable challenges of the industries.

#### The primary objectives are:

The value added courses aim to make our students to keep pace with the cutting-edge technologies pertaining to their chosen field of engineering.

- To supplement the curriculum for preparing the students as best to meet industry demands

- To impart professional knowledge with relevant certifications to increase employability of the students.

- To help our students gain exposure to the latest in technological developments and to provide an opportunity to develop inter-disciplinary skills

#### VOCATIONAL COURSES

The vocational courses aspire to equip rural persons with practical skills for a specific profession or field. These are tailor-made courses to make them completely job ready. Hence, are habitually aimed at a focused career and intended in a manner such as to help them upgrade their skills for that particular profession.

In Vocational Courses, learning is imparted mainly through practical on-site experience and less through classroom teaching. The course is planned in a manner that when the students graduate they are totally prepared for the particular job and necessitate not much training in the basic functioning of things.

#### The primary objectives are:

- To enhance the employability of unemployed youths through skill development in selected areas.

- To bridge the gap between demand and supply of skilled workforce in the industrial sector.

- To provide sustainable employment opportunities to the needy and the vulnerable unemployed rural youths.

- To disseminate technical knowledge and appropriate skill practices through standard systems of training, testing and certification to validate proficiency levels.

### Sports Day – 2020

- Events college , Sports

- March 17, 2020

The Sixth Annual Sports Day of AAA College of Engineering & Technology, Sivakasi was conducted on 13 th March, 2020. The programme began with the invocation of Tamil Thai Vaazhthu followed by the Flag hoisting ceremony. Mr. M. Joseph Andrew, IV ECE welcomed the gathering. The National Flag was hoisted by our honourable Chief Guest for the day, Dr. M. Gopinath, Deputy Director of Physical Education, University College of Engineering, BIT Campus, Anna University, Tiruchirappalli. Our esteemed Correspondent Dr. P. Ganesan hoisted the Olympic Flag following which the College Flag was hoisted by our respected Joint Secretary, Dr. K. Vignesh Kumar.

The athletes and players of our College performed the Parade and our Chief Guest Dr. M. Gopinath accepted the Salute of the athletes. The Sixth annual Sport Day was declared open by the Chief Guest and the Olympic torch was carried around the 400 m track by the best Anna University Zone 17 representatives of our College. The Olympic flame was lit by M. Suresh of IV year Mechanical Engineering accompanied by B. Sarath Raja (IV EEE), M. Prabhu (IV CSE), M. Periyasamy (IV Mechanical), M. Arun Sathish (III ECE), G.M. Jeyashakkiya (II ECE), P. Varun Kumar (III ECE), P. Indhu (IV ECE) and G. Ram Prasadh (IV EEE).The Leader and Captains of the parade, K. Arun (IV Mechanical), M. Kalirajan (III Mechanical), M.B. Dheeban Sujai (III Mechanical), M. Sathiesh Pandian (III Mechanical) and G. Surya Prakash (III ECE) were the Olympic Oath takers.

The track events namely 100 mts dash, 4×400 mts relay and 4×100 mts relay were conducted, besides which students also performed traditional Indian martial arts like Rope Gymnastics, Mallakhamb Gymnastics and Silambam. The final event on the ground was the Closing dance performed by athletes and players. Concurrently, the winners of the various individual track and field events like 100 mts, 200 mts, 400 mts, 1500 mts, 5000 mts, Long jump, High jump, Triple Jump, Shot put, Discus throw and Javelin throw under both boys and girls category were honoured by the Chief Guest, Trust members, Management members, Principal and HODs at the Victory Stand.

Sekar, Trust members Mrs. Grahalakshmi Karvannan, Mrs. Sasimala Ganesan and Mr. Amarnath Ganesan distributed medals, trophies and certificates to the winners and runners of all the team games.

### Digital Journalism

AAA College of Engineering & Technology in association with Digital Journalist Association of India organized a one day workshop on Digital Journalism and launched DIJAI Students Forum on Saturday 24th March 2018. Dr. P. Ganesan, Mg. Director, Vinayaga Sony Fireworks Group, and Correspondent of AAA College of Engineering & Technology presided over the programme. Around 400 students from Virudhunagar District Arts and Science, Engineering and Polytechnic Colleges attended the programme.

Dr. Santhosh Babu IAS, Chairman & MD, Tamil Nadu Handicrafts Development Corporation and OSD, Chief Ministers Special Cell, Government of Tamil Nadu inaugurated the programme. He enumerated the key factors of success: be a creative thinker; voracious reader; and an effective communicator. He educated the students to resist temptation and lead their lives as leaders.

Ms. Susan Koshy, Editor in Chief, PreSense, and Secretary, DiJAI enlightened the audience on Editing + Importance of brevity, grammar, and language. She explained how meticulous one has to be while drafting the content for digital media. Such a well-organized content needs to be free of grammatical inaccuracy. She quoted that reliability is the strong suit of a writer.

Mr. R Nurullah, a Senior Tamil journalist, and Vice President, DiJAI presented a topic on Writing for Tamil media and ethical practices. The session was fun-filled with the captivating speech of Dinamalar famous Editor of “Tea Kadai Bench”. He made the audience realize how important it is to visualize the target audience and their needs.

Mr. V. Rajendran, Cyber Advocate, and Chairman, Digital Security Association of India (DiSAI) gave a speech on Cyber Law affecting the Journalism. He showed light on the freedom of expression and the cyber laws. He insisted on the inevitable presence of ethics and morality in presenting a digital content.

Mr. Vinoth Poovalingam, CEO, Hocalwire, Delhi (through teleconference) explained Global trends in Digital Journalism. He projected the gradual growth of the history of journalism over the decades. He also pointed out that the Indian internet users are around 438 million and said that there is a great impact in the society by the social media and chat applications.

Ms. Vidyashree Dharmaraj, Editor-in-Chief, Covai Post, Coimbatore (through teleconference) elucidated Challenges in Digital Journalism. She expounded her real-life challenges. Her speech focused on the unpredictable external threats for a journalist.

The technical sessions were succeeded by a Feedback session and an awe-inspiring response from the students.

There is no field left across the globe where one cannot find the usage of electronics and communication engineering. It has got wide application in Industries.
