Workshop practices have become important in the industrial environment to produce products for the service of mankind. The knowledge of manufacturing practices is highly essential for all engineers and technocrats for familiarizing themselves with modern concepts of manufacturing technologies. Workshop practices gives the basic working knowledge required for the production of various engineering products. It explains the construction, function, use and application of different working tools, equipment, machines, as well as the technique of manufacturing a product from its raw material. Considering the general needs of engineering students in the country and the fact that they hardly get any exposure to hand tools, equipment’s, machines and manufacturing setups, a basic course in manufacturing science remains a core subject for all the branches of engineering. The contents include exposure to bench work and fitting, smithy and forging, sheet metal work, wood and wood working, casting, welding and machine shop practices. LATHE

Manufacturing processes are used for converting raw materials into finished products. Various processes, machinery, and operations will be examined with emphasis placed on understanding engineering materials and processing parameters that influence design considerations, product quality, and production costs. The objective of this laboratory is to study and practice the various machining operations like Taper Turning, External Thread cutting, Internal Thread Cutting, Eccentric Turning & Knurling in lathe, and to equip with the practical knowledge required in the core industries. The work benches are built with safety and the shop is large enough to carry out the machining and manufacturing processes comfortably. The exercises will help the students to produce components as per the given drawing using lathe machine, also to develop the basic machine ability concepts and improve the teamwork and entrepreneurial skills.

Graphic Design is the art of profession of visual communication that combines images, words and ideas to convey information to an audience especially to produce a specific effect. In other words Graphic Design is a communication Design – way of conveying ideas through visuals and design.

Multimedia is the second aspect of the graphic design industry. It allows the student to create the interactive visuals essential in today’s digital advertising. This workshop prepares an individual to make a career in graphics, web designing, print and publishing. It trains students in understanding how images, words, symbols and letters can used as effective means of communication and portray the right message to the right audience at the right time.

This prepares students to work with solid design concepts and take their ideas into full production using computers equipped with the industry current graphic design capabilities.

- CE3413 – Soil Mechanics Laboratory (II year – IV Semester)

The knowledge of the Soil Mechanics Laboratory is necessary for all Civil Engineering works as the determination of the engineering properties of soils plays an important role in all types of construction.

The following are the main objectives of this laboratory:

- To determine the classification of soil into silt, sand and clay etc.

- To determine the Index and Engineering properties of soil like specific gravity, water content, shrinkage limit, plastic limit, permeability, consolidation, shear strength tests etc.

The knowledge gained from this laboratory will be useful to understand the theoretical subjects like Soil Mechanics and Foundation Engineering. This laboratory is also useful in the field of structural design of sub structures like footings, pile foundations and retaining walls.

### About the Department

Department of Science and Humanities is the foundation of engineering education. In our Department the ethos of science and technology regains, as it is believed that Engineering and Science are, by their very nature, humanistic and socially derived enterprises.

We strongly believe that engineering education is twined with basic sciences. It is indeed the prime option for any engineering discipline. Every student uses the equipments and is not just passive observers as student’s hands-on experience is valued very highly.

An environment that combines friendly atmosphere with leading-edge facilities characterizes the department. The flagship objective of the Department is to train the young minds to explore the new horizons.

English language is ubiquitous and spoken throughout the world. It is the language for all walks of life. A good command and communication in English are essential in the modern world to wield not only respect but in all business transactions. The Department of English is fully equipped with erudite faculty, a good language laboratory and other infrastructure to impart the language skills effectively.

Mathematics, the queen of sciences, is the basis for all branches of Science, Engineering and Technology. Any complex ideas can be logically expressed by equations and formulae. Mathematics itself is a language through which difficult problems can be addressed.

The study of Physics uncovers the mysteries of nature through the knowledge of properties of matter. In the Physics laboratory adequate equipment and instruments are available for performing all types of experiments involving light and other forms of energy.

The study of Chemistry is crucial in all manufacturing processes where the transformation of one form of material into another. Equally important is the study of Environmental Chemistry and Engineering, to save the globe from pollutions.

The Odore Von Karman remarked that a scientist is one who “seeks to understand what is” and an engineer is one who “Seeks to create what never was “.

#### Vision

To heighten the theoretical framework and methodology of basic sciences and to acuminate computational clouts, logical thinking, designing abilities and problem solving intellects of the students to build disciplined successful and socially pledged technocrats.

#### Mission

To evolve technical and communicative skills to prepare the students for industry needs

To cater excellent academic ambience for professional development of the students.

To create passion for learning Science, Engineering and Technology by conferring quality education to the students.

- Platform: HackPy

Embedded systems lab helps the students to improve their knowledge on architecture, programming and interfacing of several processors and microcontrollers. The features and facilities available in this lab help the students to do their projects and enhance their knowledge on the latest trends and technologies. Students should be able to understand the basic components of a computer, write C language programs that perform I/O functions and implement simple data structures, manipulate numbers in multiple formats, and understand how software uses global memory to store permanent information and the stack to store temporary information. The objective of the lab is

- To enable the students to program, simulate and test the ARM processor based circuits and their interfaces

- To enable the students to program various devices using KIEL software

- To provide a platform for the students to do multidisciplinary projects

- To gain experience in programming languages that are used in current industrial practice

Lab Courses Handled in the Lab:

Course Code: CE 3481 | Course Name: Strength of Materials & Fluid Mechanics and Machines Laboratory | Year & Semester: II & IV

This lab is run in conjunction with the theory course Fluid Mechanics and Machinery. It is an introductory course where flow behavior, fluid forces and analysis tools are introduced. The goals of the experiments include determination of forces generated when fluid flow takes place over a solid object, applications of the control volume approach, demonstration of the momentum and energy equations, viscosity measurement and engineering correlations. Experimental setups such as flow through a tube, flow over a flat plate, orifice-meter, roto-meter, determination of friction factor through pipes and viscometer are made available to the students. The lab experiments utilize U-tube manometer and digital manometer to measure the pressure difference between the systems. The lab runs closely with the lectures in such a way that experiments support the text covered in the class room. The element of the turbine machine is common for all turbine machines and is called an impeller, also turbine wheel, rotor, screw or runner. Additionally, students are learning about turbine machines like pumps, fans, compressors, water turbines, gas turbines, steam turbines, wind turbines, etc.

### Blood Donation Camp on 02.03.19

- Events college , NSS , Rotaract

- March 1, 2019

The ROTARACT CLUB, YOUTH RED CROSS CLUB and NSS unit of AAA College of Engineering and Technology, Sivakasiorganiseda “ Voluntary Blood Donation Camp” for all students and staff in association with Government Hospital, Virudhunagar and Primary Health Centre Amathur.

The programme was inaugurated by Dr.M.Sekar, Principal AAACET and Dr.M.Parthasarathy, MBBS, DCP, and Dr.N.Bindhu, MBBS. They emphasised that blood donation is one of the most significant contributions that a person can make towards the society.

They encouraged students to donate Blood as it is not harmful and the body of the donor can regenerate the blood within a few days. More than 100 volunteers came forward to donate blood and 100units of blood were collected by officials. The donors were provided with a certificate.

### Logo Design Event on 11-10-2025

- October 14, 2025

The Department of Artificial Intelligence and Data Science successfully organised a Logo Design Competition on October 11, 2025, from 2:00 p.m. to 3:30 p.m., exclusively for AI & DS students, which aimed to encourage creativity, innovation, and design thinking. Participants enthusiastically used the Canva platform on their own laptops to visually express their ideas, strictly without the use of AI editing tools, and were required to present the concept behind their designs. The judging panel praised the impressive and original logos that effectively captured the themes of AI and Data Science, highlighting the students’ innovative ideas and clarity of presentation. The event saw active involvement, concluding successfully with the announcement of the winners and the award of a ₹500 cash prize to the best logo designer, ultimately enhancing the students’ creative confidence.

The Programming Laboratory – I is a dedicated computing facility established to provide first-year students with a strong foundation in programming, computational thinking, and problem-solving skills. The laboratory supports practical learning in fundamental programming concepts through hands-on experience in C Programming, Python Programming, Essentials of Computing, Data Structures, and Object-Oriented Programming. Students are trained to design algorithms, develop programs, debug errors, implement data structures, and solve real-world computational problems using modern programming tools and techniques.

The laboratory is supported by a centralized Data Centre, and all systems are interconnected through a high-speed Local Area Network (LAN), enabling efficient resource sharing and seamless access to computing resources. The facility is equipped with 33 computer systems, 1 Epson Dot Matrix Printer, high-speed internet connectivity, and operates in a fully air-conditioned environment with 5 KVA UPS power backup to ensure uninterrupted laboratory sessions.

To facilitate programming and software development activities, the laboratory provides access to software tools such as Code::Blocks IDE and Python, enabling students to develop, compile, execute, test, and debug programs effectively. The laboratory offers practical exposure to structured programming, object-oriented programming, data structures, algorithm development, and data science fundamentals, thereby bridging the gap between theoretical concepts and real-world implementation.

### TB AWARENESS DRIVE on 09-10-2025

- October 10, 2025

On October 9, 2025, the NSS Unit of AAACET organized a significant awareness session under the Mithra TB Initiative, aimed at educating students and the public about Tuberculosis (TB) care and prevention. The event featured an enlightening address by the Chief Guest, Mr.M.Prabhakaran, Senior Treatment Supervisor of Virudhunagar Block. With his extensive experience in TB care, he provided NSS volunteers with a comprehensive overview of the protocols followed in managing TB cases. His insights emphasized the importance of timely medical intervention and adherence to prescribed medication, which are critical to controlling the spread of the disease. The Chief Guest also highlighted various government schemes and support systems available for TB patients, encouraging volunteers to act as ambassadors of public health. He urged them to disseminate this knowledge within their communities, helping to break the stigma surrounding TB and promote early detection and treatment. At the end of the session, four NSS volunteers enrolled themselves as ambassadors of the Mithra TB Initiative. The program was coordinated by NSS Coordinator Mr.S.Balamurugan.

### Texas Instruments Innovation Lab

AAACET – Texas Instruments University Program aims to bridge the gap between the worlds of business and academia, bringing real world engineering concepts to life.

#### Texas Instruments Innovation Lab

The Texas Instruments Innovation Lab (TIIL) creates a technical education ecosystem at your campus that connects industry and academia, bringing real-world engineering concepts to life. In our view, today’s students are the engineers of tomorrow. They need hands-on design experience and experiential learning to master the basics and start their careers. Students are encouraged to consider different approaches and quickly explore them in an open and collaborative environment. It lets you experiment, innovate, and solve real-world problems. Product ideas are incubated and quickly tested in the TII lab. This lab connects TI platforms and students and discovers new technology uses in engineering

#### Objectives

- Provide students with practical experience in programming and interfacing with microcontrollers MSP430,432 Launch pad, and Trainer kit.

- Develop skills in wireless communication protocols and technologies through the use of RF Booster packs.

- Teach students the fundamentals of real-time signal processing and its applications using DSP processors – TMS320C6678.

- Equip students with skills and knowledge relevant to the embedded systems industry, preparing them for careers in this field.

#### Features

- TI innovation lab trains and gives hands-on experience for students and faculty with latest products of Texas Instruments used in industry.

- TI innovation lab empowers students and faculty to showcase their innovations in terms of projects and products.

- TI innovation lab provides opportunity to the faculty and student to work on the Industry 4.0 technology, Advanced Digital Signal Processors and latest Embedded processing technology.

- TI innovation lab enables faculty and students to do research and develop solutions to the industry problems in collaboration with industry.

### Entrepreneurship Development Cell

EDC aims at bridging the gap between the stage wherein one seeds in an idea and the stage where one can actually implement it if it can benefit the present needs of the society

### History of EDC at AAACET

The Entrepreneurship Development Cell of AAACET was established on January 27, 2014, with a MOU signed between Native Lead Foundation, Madurai. The Entrepreneurship Development Cell at AAACET aims at manifesting the latent Entrepreneurial spirit of young students.

Here at the Cell, we aim at bridging the gap between the stage wherein one seeds in an idea and the stage where one can actually implement it if it can benefit the present needs of the society. Moreover to provide the safe, secure and protected environment within college campus, EDC will provide all the necessary support to the students who want to start their outfit. AAACET calls their budding and bright stars as “Edu-preneurs”.

### Objective

- To forge tie ups with various Corporates engaged into Entrepreneurship development for mentoring.

- To conduct orientation programmes for students and to attract them into establishing their own enterprises.

- To organize programmes for Girls for acquiring special skills So that they can earn while at home.

- To organize workshops participating successful entrepreneurs.

- To provide assistance to budding entrepreneurs in getting bank loans, selection of human resources and dealing with day-to-day problems in their business.

### Inaugural of E-Cell

On July 24, 2018 the E-cell activities for the academic year 2018-2019 with the second batch students was inaugurated by our Principal Dr.M.Sekar. The Principal delivered the inaugural speech motivating the students with success stories of entrepreneurs. He advised the students to participate actively in the E-Cell Activities as well as in the curriculum.

Followed by his speech, Ms.R.Renita Rexy , EDC Coordinator, welcomed the gathering and explained the role of EDC and listed out various activities we have done and planned in this academic year.

Course Code: ME8512 | Course Name: Thermal Engineering laboratory | Year & Semester: III & V

The main objective of this Heat Transfer lab is to impart practical knowledge on heat transfer, mass transfer in engineering systems. In this lab the students will do the experiments related to their subjects like thermodynamics, thermal engineering, heat and mass transfer concepts. This lab provides a facility to conduct the experiments on a wide range of problems involving thermal conductivity of the specimen by two slab guarded hot plate method using Guarded plate apparatus, rate of heat transfer through different layers of composite wall, the heat transfer coefficient under natural convection and forced convection, finding StefanBoltzman constant, overall heat transfer co-efficient in parallel flow and counter flow heat exchanger apparatus. Thermal conductivity of different insulating materials using LAGGED PIPE apparatus, determination of temperature distribution of a PIN-FIN for forced convection and FIN efficiency using Pin-fin apparatus, measure the emissivity of the test plate surface using Emissivity measurement apparatus are some of the experiments related to heat transfer. Through this lab, students will get practical exposure and methods to capable of bringing solutions to practical and industrial problems.

A one day industrial visit was arranged for the students of II-year EEE (48 Students) on 14.11.2022 (Monday). They visited V.V.V & Sons (P) Ltd., Virudhunagar in the morning session followed by the 1MW Solar power plant, Kurunaikulam in afternoon. The visit was very informative to the students in the view of understanding the process of extracting the oil and they had seen the different types of machinery used in this process. In Forenoon Session, students visited Solar Power Plant, Kurunaikulam. In that session, the company person delivered the details of the plant; then, they introduced the step-by-step process of the solar power generation at the plant, from sunlight capture to electricity distribution.

### Institution’s Innovation Council

The primary mandate of MIC is to encourage, inspire and nurture young students by supporting them to work with new ideas and transform them into prototypes while they are informative years.

#### Institution’s Innovation Council (IIC), AAACET (IC201912025)

Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD), Govt. of India has established ‘MHRD’s Innovation Cell (MIC)’ to systematically foster the culture of Innovation amongst all Higher Education Institutions (HEIs).

The primary mandate of MIC is to encourage, inspire and nurture young students by supporting them to work with new ideas and transform them into prototypes while they are informative years.

MIC has envisioned encouraging creation of ‘Institution’s Innovation Council (IICs)’ across selected HEIs. A network of these IICs will be established to promote innovation in the Institution through multitudinous modes leading to an innovation promotion eco-system in the campuses.

#### History of IIC

AAACET established the Institutions’ Innovation Council (IIC) on 17.09.2019 and conducting various activities as per the guidelines from the Ministry of Education, Govt. of India, to promote innovation eco-system between the student and faculty community. Secured 3.5 STAR during Academic year – 2019-2020.

#### Major focus of IIC

- To create a vibrant local innovation ecosystem.

- Start-up supporting Mechanism in HEIs.

- Prepare institute for Atal Ranking of Institutions on Innovation Achievements Framework.

- Establish Function Ecosystem for Scouting Ideas and Pre-incubation of Ideas. Develop better Cognitive Ability for Technology Students.

#### Functions of IICs

- To conduct various innovation and entrepreneurship-related activities prescribed by Central MIC in time bound fashion.

- Identify and reward innovations and share success stories.

- Organize periodic workshops/ seminars/ interactions with entrepreneurs, investors, professionals and create a mentor pool for student innovators.

- Network with peers and national entrepreneurship development organizations.

- Create an Institution’s Innovation portal to highlight innovative projects carried out by institution’s faculty and students.

- Organize Hackathons, idea competition, mini-challenges etc. with the involvement of industries.

Internet Programming refers to the writing, mark-up and coding involved in web development, which includes web content, web client and server scripting and network security. The most common languages used for web programming are XML, HTML, JavaScript, Perl 5 and PHP. An Internet Application is a client server application that uses standard internet protocols for connecting the client to the server. In computing, a web application or web app is a client-server computer program which the client runs in a web browser. Common web applications include webmail, online retail sales, online auctions, wikis, instant messaging services and many other functions.

The Department of Computer Science and Engineering has a well-established Internet Programming Laboratory. This laboratory provides essential facilities to the students to enhance their knowledge in Internet Programming, Java Programming, Cloud computing, Database Management Systems, Security, Object Oriented Analysis & Design and Mobile Application Development. The laboratory is supported by Data centre and all computers in this laboratory are connected to the Data centre via N500W WIFI with LAN.

The laboratory is well equipped with 33 Dell PCs, 1 and an internet facility in an Air Conditioned Environment.

A Software Engineering Laboratory is a state-of-the-art facility designed to bridge the gap between theoretical concepts and real-world software development practices. It serves as a dedicated environment where students learn, apply, and master the principles of software engineering throughout the entire software development life cycle (SDLC) — from requirements gathering and system design to coding, testing, deployment, and maintenance.

Software Engineering has evolved from traditional programming into a disciplined, systematic, and quantifiable engineering approach to developing high-quality, reliable, scalable, and maintainable software systems. The modern demand is for robust, maintainable, and secure software solutions delivered within time and budget constraints. A Software Engineering Laboratory provides hands-on experience with industry-standard processes, tools, and methodologies to meet these challenges effectively.

### ABOUT THE CLUB

Since 2022, The Society of Automotive Engineers (SAE) Collegiate Club has been functioning successfully in our college. Presently, the club has around 74 members from Mechanical department and 2 faculty advisors. The club is very keen in encouraging the young minds in the fields of automotive engineering. The NSS unit of AAA College of Engineering and Technology proudly organized the “Har Ghar Tiranga” campaign, a patriotic initiative that united our campus community in celebrating the glory of the Indian National Flag.

NSS volunteers Antony Raja A, Ezhilarasan S, Suriya Prakash K, Ripudhaman M, and Neethiselvan C took the lead in this inspiring event, where they eloquently explained the rich history and significance of our Tricolor. - EC 8761 – Advanced Communication Laboratory (IV Year – VII Semester)

Advanced Communication Laboratory covers design and verification of concept of modern communication systems that operates in MHz- THz range. The main objective of advanced communication laboratory is to design and develop RF/antenna modules, modulation schemes, parametric characterization of wireless modules, software defined radio applications, different wireless standards and work on research problems and innovative projects that extend the state of art of wireless systems. The laboratory experiments are designed to give the students ability to design, build and analyze the components. The first part of the course uses optical bench setup which consist of advanced optical fiber trainer kits for determination of numerical aperture, attenuation and losses of fiber. The second part of the course uses advanced optical fiber trainer kit for conducting PC to PC communication, BER measurement ,pulse broadening. The third part of the course uses microwave bench setup which consist of X band frequency range of microwave components for carrying mode characteristics, V-I characteristics of microwave passive and active devices.

### VALIANT 2020 NATIONAL LEVEL SYMPOSIUM on 31.01.2020

The Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering of AAA College of Engineering and Technology successfully organized the National Level Technical Symposium “VALIANT 2020” on 31.01.2020 in the college campus.

Dr. S. Arumuga Perumal, Associate Professor & Head, Department of CSE, S.T. Hindu College, Nagarcoil was the chief Guest of the day for the event “ VALIANT 2020 ” . The event took place in the presence of Principal, Heads of various Department, faculty members and students.

The event started by lighting the kuthuvilaku by the dignitaries. Mr.M.Marees kumar, (Fourth year ECE) the student president, Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering extended a warm greeting to the delightful gathering.

Principal Dr. M.Sekar while delivering the presidential address shared the importance of IOT and explains the steps taken by AAACET to build IOT lab for training the students felicitated for the successful conduction of symposium. The Chief Guest, Virudhunagar District Revenue Officer Mrs.Anandhi, urged the students to cast their votes without fail in the upcoming election on April 23, 2026, and to encourage their friends and relatives to participate in the electoral process. Mrs.Subavasugi, Deputy Director of Horticulture (DDH), explained the fundamental necessity of voting for a country’s development. To inspire the gathering, NSS Volunteer Mr.R.Santhakumar performed an awareness song highlighting the significance of voting. ### VOTER AWARENESS PROGRAM on 08-03-2024

- March 12, 2024

The NSS unit of AAACET successfully organized a comprehensive voter awareness program on March 8, 2024. The campaign featured a series of informative sessions conducted by dedicated NSS volunteers. They highlighted the democratic principles that underpin our nation and the crucial role that voting plays in shaping its future. The volunteers explained how voting empowers citizens to choose their representatives and influence government policies. All participating students took a solemn pledge to exercise their right to vote in future elections and to encourage others to do the same. The pledge reinforced the commitment of the students to active citizenship and their belief in the power of democracy. The online quiz served as a fun and engaging way to reinforce the concepts discussed in the seminar and encourage further learning. This program was coordinated by the NSS unit coordinator, Mr.S.Balamurugan.

### Nasa Space Apps Bootcamp on 21.09.2023

- September 20, 2023

AAA College of Engineering and Technology organizing Nasa Space Apps Bootcamp on 21.09.2023.

The NASA International Space Apps Challenge (or Space Apps) is an international hackathon that will take place virtually and in person over a 2 day period for cities around the globe between October 7th and 8th, 2023. Since its inception in 2012, NASA’s International Space Apps Challenge has engaged 220,000+ registrants from 185+countries/territories in using NASA’s open data to build innovative solutions to challenges we face on Earth and in space. The event embraces collaborative problem solving with a goal of producing open-source solutions to challenges we currently face on Earth and in space. Space Apps is open to the public and free for all ages to attend. Space Apps is open to creatives, storytellers, and anyone with a passion and desire to have an immediate impact on the world.For each year’s NASA International Space Apps Challenge, NASA designs challenges, and we (the Global Organizing Team) work with local hosts (Local Leads) around the world to implement events where teams work intensively to design solutions over the course of a 2 day period. Space Apps gives participants the opportunity to bring projects to life for a wide range of applications. We are looking forward to seeing what innovative, creative ideas participants are brought to the community this year. Space Apps is the global community’s chance to experience, experiment, and explore solutions to our universe’s biggest challenges!.As the countdown to the twelfth year of Space Apps continues, we are increasingly eager to have problem-solvers of all walks of life join us on the journey, whether hosting a Space Apps event in their community, rolling up their sleeves and participating, or helping students, professionals, engineers, makers, artists, coders, and storytellers on their intrepid travels into Space Apps.

### One Day Industrial Visit on 13.03.2026

- March 16, 2026

An industrial visit was organized for the II year students on 13.03.2026 with a total of 41 participants. The visit aimed to provide practical exposure to industrial operations and enhance students’ understanding of real-world manufacturing and printing processes.

The students visited Penguin Apparels Private Limited, located at Kanniseri, Sivakasi. During the visit, students observed various stages of garment production, including fabric processing, stitching, quality control, and packaging. The technical staff explained the workflow, machinery used, and quality assurance practices followed in the industry.

The second visit was to Nadar Press Limited, Sivakasi. Here, students gained insights into modern printing technologies, offset printing processes, and large-scale production techniques. The industry experts elaborated on printing methods, color management, and safety measures implemented in the plant.

Overall, the industrial visit was highly informative and beneficial. It helped bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical application, giving students valuable exposure to industrial environments and processes.

### Teachers’ day celebration on 09-09-2025

The Department of Information Technology, through its vibrant association TechNexus, proudly organized the Teachers’ Day Celebration on September 9, 2025 with immense enthusiasm and gratitude. The day turned out to be truly special for both the students and faculty members, as it brought everyone together in a warm and memorable atmosphere filled with respect, kindness, and joy.

On this occasion, all the faculty members from different departments visited the classrooms and delivered thoughtful speeches. Their words, filled with kindness and motivation, inspired the students to aim high, work hard, and shape a brighter future. The heartfelt speeches reminded everyone of the invaluable role that teachers play in guiding, mentoring, and shaping young minds with patience and dedication.

Students, in turn, expressed their deep appreciation and gratitude towards their beloved teachers. They conveyed their feelings through touching words, heartfelt thanks, and small tokens of love in the form of gifts. The faculty members happily accepted these gestures, which symbolized the students’ respect and affection. This exchange created an emotional bond that highlighted the true essence of Teachers’ Day—celebrating the relationship between students and teachers.

The entire celebration was filled with laughter, emotions, and a sense of togetherness. Every moment of the day was memorable, from the inspiring speeches to the joyous exchanges between teachers and students. The event concluded in an atmosphere of peace, joy, and heartfelt happiness, leaving behind cherished memories for everyone present.

The Teachers’ Day celebration organized by TechNexus, Department of Information Technology, truly stood out as a day of gratitude, inspiration, and togetherness.

It was a reminder that while teachers are the guiding lights of knowledge, students’ love and respect make their journey even more rewarding. This celebration will forever remain etched in the hearts of the IT family as a day that honored wisdom, kindness, and the everlasting bond between teachers and students.

page_title: CSIR Sponsored Seminar on Deep Learning
text:
### CSIR Sponsored Seminar on Deep Learning

- March 26, 2019

Department of Computer Science and Engineering organizes CSIR Sponsored Two Days National Seminar on Deep Learning for Medical Image Analysis – Challenges and Future on 29th and 30th April 2019.

Deep learning algorithms have the potential to be invested deeply in all fields of medicine, from drug discovery to clinical decision making, significantly altering the way medicine is practiced. The success of deep learning algorithms in recent years comes at an opportune time when medical records are increasingly digitalized. Medical images are an integral part of a patient’s electronic health records and are currently analysed by human radiologists, who are limited by speed, fatigue, and experience. It takes years and great financial cost to train a qualified radiologist, and some health-care systems outsource radiology reporting to lower-cost countries such as India via tele-radiology. A delayed or erroneous diagnosis causes harm to the patient. Therefore, it is ideal for medical image analysis to be carried out by an automated, accurate and efficient deep learning algorithm.

This seminar will focus on how Deep Learning can be utilized for addressing some important problems in medical image analysis.

### DIGITAL LITERACY TRAINING on 27-09-2025

- October 3, 2025

The NSS Unit of AAACET conducted a Digital Literacy Training Program for the students of Hajee P Syed Mohammad Higher Secondary School, Virudhunagar, on 27th September 2025. The session was led by enthusiastic NSS Volunteers, who introduced students to essential digital skills, including basic computer operations, document creation and editing, and smart document preparation using Gemini AI. Students actively engaged with the tools and expressed their excitement about using technology in their daily lives. Feedback from the participants was overwhelmingly positive, highlighting the clarity of instruction, relevance of content, and the supportive environment created by the volunteers. The event reinforced AAACET’s commitment to community outreach and digital inclusion, aligning with the broader goals of the NSS. The program was coordinated by NSS Coordinator Mr. S. Balamurugan.

### ECE Parents Teachers Meeting on 05-10-2024

The Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering conducted Parents – Teachers Meeting on 05-10-2024 Saturday @ 11.00AM in the Thomas Alva Edison Hall. Dr.T.Senthil HOD/ECE welcomed the parents and briefed about the academic activities organized in the previous year & placement achievements .61 Parents of ECE students attended the PTA meeting. The mentors of the respective students discussed the academic performance of the students with the parents, including the attendance percentage of the students up to this week, internal tests -1 & 2 Marks and Anna University April /May 2024 Result. The parents also interacted with the faculty in the meeting and feedback was also collected. The Anna University Result Toppers appreciated with the shields in the presence of their parents.

### ECE Symposium VALIANT’2022 on 14.10.2022

- October 22, 2022

Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering, AAA College of Engineering and Technology, Sivakasi, in association with IETE Student Forum organized “National Level Technical Symposium – VALIANT’2022 on 14.10.2022. The Chief Guest of the function was Mr.B.Sankar Madaswamy, Scientist / Engineer – SF, Manager, HRD, ISRO Telemetry Tracking and Command Network (ISTRAC), Bangalore. The Function started with a prayer song and Mr. R. Suriyamoorthy, Second Year ECE welcomed the gathering. Dr. S. Sevugarajan, Professor and Head, Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering gave the inaugural address and briefed about the professional laboratories in the department apart from the Anna University curriculum. He also informed the students that the workshops will be conducted at these laboratories during the symposium. Ms. R. Oviya of Third year Electronics and Communication Engineering introduced the chief guest. Dr. M. Sekar, Principal, delivered felicitation address and it was followed by presentation of a memento as a token of love and affection to the chief guest.

Mr.B.Sankar Madaswamy, during his address presented the detailed explanation about the various satellites that has been launched by ISRO and provided information about various research centre associated with ISRO such as Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC), Space Applications Centre (SAC), U R Rao Satellite Centre (URSC). He discussed about the ISRO’s various Satellite Launch Vehicles, Gagan Satellite Navigation System, Infra structure facilities of ISRO and its research findings through Chandrayan and Mangalyan space mission. More than 100 participants from various colleges are actively participated in the symposium,

Technical events such as Prototype presentation, Circuitix, Technofrenz, Best Engineer and Advertisement and Non technical events such as Memorax, Jazz on, Duo Dance Performance, Gaming and Online events such as Meme Master and Mobile Blow up were conducted were conducted for the external participants. Prototype presentation around 20 technical papers were presented by various college students in the area Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things, Automation, Block Chain, Solar Mobile Charger, etc.

Circuitix event which tests the very basics of electronics, this is an on the spot event which gives the opportunity to showcase the students skills at designing and implementing electronic circuits. First round the aptitude test, which tests the basics of digital and analog knowledge of the participants. A problem statement was provided to the participants building a circuit based on the given problem statement. The accuracy and the approach in building the circuit is observed. Technofrenz event on the spot technical topic is given to the participants after two minutes they have to talk about the topic.

Best Engineer event was conducted by to test the technical and managerial skill of the students.

The Cloud Computing and Security Laboratory is a specialized computing facility designed to provide students with practical exposure to cloud technologies, virtualization platforms, cybersecurity principles, and secure computing environments. The laboratory enables learners to develop, deploy, manage, and secure cloud-based applications while gaining hands-on experience in modern cloud infrastructure and information security practices.

The laboratory supports practical sessions for courses such as Cloud Computing, Cloud Services Management, Software Defined Networks, Data Science Laboratory, Compiler Design, UI & UX Design, Digital Marketing, and Ethics and AI, thereby providing a multidisciplinary environment for learning emerging technologies. Students are trained in cloud service models, virtualization techniques, network management, secure application deployment, data protection mechanisms, and security best practices in distributed computing environments.

The facility is equipped with 33 computer systems consisting of HP monitors and Dell Core i5 processors, supported by a 5 KVA UPS for uninterrupted operation. The laboratory provides a reliable computing environment for conducting experiments related to cloud platforms, virtual machines, network configuration, data analytics, secure software development, and AI-enabled applications.

To facilitate practical learning, the laboratory is equipped with industry-relevant software tools including VirtualBox, Python, Anaconda, NetBeans IDE, Code::Blocks IDE, and Figma. These tools enable students to create virtualized environments, develop cloud-based solutions, perform data analysis, design user interfaces, implement secure applications, and explore emerging computing paradigms.

The primary objective of the Cloud Computing and Security Laboratory is to bridge the gap between theoretical concepts and real-world implementation by providing hands-on experience in cloud infrastructure management, cybersecurity practices, virtualization technologies, network services, and secure application development. The laboratory also promotes innovation, research, and skill development in emerging domains such as cloud-native computing, software-defined networking, data analytics, artificial intelligence, and digital transformation technologies.

A Data Science lab is a designated data science system that is intended to uncover all that your data has to offer. As a space that facilitates data science and accelerates data experimentation, data labs uncover which questions businesses should ask, then help to find the answer.

Data Science has evolved from a specialized computer application to a central component of a modern computing environment and as a result knowledge about has become an essential part of computer science. A data Science is computer application software that provides a way to manage data. The requirement of modern days is to have an automated system that manages, modifies and updates data accurately. This is achieved by a Data science in robust, correct and non redundant way. Data Science and data analytics laboratory aims at practicing and achieving this aim by using various software’s such as VirtualBox, NetBeans, etc. The laboratory is supported by Data centre and all computers in this laboratory are connected to the Data centre via LAN.

The laboratory is well equipped with 33 Thin Client systems, and an internet facility in an Air-Conditioned Environment with 5 KVA power backup facilities. The primary objective of data science is to identify patterns in data. It analyses the data and derives insights using a variety of statistical techniques. A data scientist must carefully examine the data after data extraction, wrangling, and pre-processing.

- October 15, 2022

In AAA College of Engineering and Technology, Sivakasi, the Department of Computer Science and Engineering in association with CSI Student Chapter organized “National Level Technical Symposium – AUGUSTA 2K22” on 23.09.2022. The Chief Guest for the function was Mr. G. Aravindraj, Founder and CEO of Nminds Academy, Erode. The function started with a prayer song. Ms. P. Vasantha Devi, Student Coordinator – Augusta 2k22, Department of Computer Science and Engineering welcomed the gathering. Dr.J.Sutha, Professor and Head, Department of Computer Science and Engineering gave the inaugural address and briefed about the events of symposium to the participants. Ms. I. Jemimah Blessingta of Final year Computer Science and Engineering, introduced the chief guest to the participants. Dr. J. Sutha, Professor and Head, Department of Computer Science and Engineering, presented a memento as a token of love and affection to our chief guest. In the chief guest address, he presented the skills needed to get a job in IT sector and insist the participants to improve their skills to succeed in their career. More than 200 participants from various engineering and arts colleges actively participated in the symposium. Technical events like Quiz -o- Grand, Code art 368, Track & Trail, 2k22 Presenter and non-technical events like Beat Beast, Strike’A Pose, Stress Manager, Mad Food Challenge were conducted in a grand manner in order to enhance the skills of students.

The programme was well organised by our Secretary Dr. P. Karvannan., Correspondent Dr. P. Ganesan., Joint Secretary Dr. K. Vignesh Kumar., Principal Dr. M. Sekar, Dr. J. Sutha, HoD/CSE, Augusta Co-ordinators Dr. P. Elamparithi, ASP/CSE, Mrs. G. Kavitha, AP/CSE and by the faculty members of CSE. During the valedictory function Dr. J. Sutha, Professor and Head, Department of Computer Science and Engineering distributed the prizes and certificates to winners. Mr. S. ### Design for Impact: Unlocking Better UI/UX

- December 12, 2025

The Department of Artificial Intelligence and Data Science at AAA College of Engineering and Technology organized a technical session titled “Design for Impact: Unlocked Better UI/UX” on October 10, 2025, for second-year students to enhance their understanding of user interface (UI) and user experience (UX) design. Led by Mr. R. K. Babin, the session started with an engaging introduction to UI/UX fundamentals, detailing the distinctions and synergistic roles of UI and UX in creating user-centred digital products, covering practical concepts like design thinking, layout planning, and colour theory using a visually rich PowerPoint presentation. ### INDUSTRY INSTITUTE PARTNERSHIP CELL

This policy outlines the objectives, functions, and responsibilities of the cell to bridge the gap between academia and industry effectively.

#### About IIPC

The Institution Industry Partnership Cell (IIPC) was established to foster a strong connection between the institute and industry, ensuring a symbiotic relationship that benefits both. This policy outlines the objectives, functions, and responsibilities of the cell to bridge the gap between academia and industry effectively.

#### Objectives

- Identify and understand industrial expectations.

- Promote institutional preparation to meet industrial needs through sponsored R&D projects, seminars, workshops, and industrial training programs.

- Contribute to the educational system by aligning academic curriculum with industry requirements.

- Equip faculty with the latest industry practices.

- Make students industry-ready by providing exposure to current industry practices and enhancing their skills to adapt to changing technologies.

- Interact with elite industries to establish partnerships

#### Functions of the IIPC

- Bridge the gap between Industry-Institute through interactive programs.

- Promote a partnership approach towards mobilizing industrial personnel.

- Arrange industrial visits for students.

- Organize seminars, symposiums, exhibitions, and workshops for faculties and students in cutting-edge technologies.

- Facilitate industrial training for students and faculty members.

- Identify opportunities for student project work in industries.

- Encourage department-level tie-ups or MoUs with industries.

- Promote consultancy activities and research and developmental activities with industry.

- Enrich the teaching-learning process through identified industrial gaps.

- Invite industry experts for guest lectures, seminars, brainstorming sessions, and expertise sharing.

#### MoU's & Industrial Visit

As an educational institution committed to providing real-world learning experiences for our students, we place great value on industry visits and interactions with professionals in the field. These unique opportunities allow our students to gain first-hand insights into the practical applications of their academic knowledge, as well as networking opportunities with industry leaders.

The objective of the laboratory is to enable the students to simulate and experiment with digital signals and systems. Digital signal processing laboratory helps the students to learn, analyses and design the techniques that give core knowledge. This Lab is concerned with the representation of signals as a sequence of numbers and the operations carried out on the signals to extract specific information contained in them. Students can implement digital signal processing algorithms using different computational platforms and DSP tools which enhance the practical exposures in signal processing.

The laboratory has both software tools and DSP processors. The laboratory has 15 user Licensed MATLAB software, with various Tool boxes and Simulink. Students simulate here number of experiments in MATLAB. Students also use Texas Instruments fixed-point and floating point Digital Signal Processor. Programing of the DSP chip is done in C(and some assembly) language using the Code Composer Studio integrated development environment.

- CE3311 – Water and Waste Water Analysis Laboratory (II year – III Semester)

The Environmental Engineering laboratory deals with the determination of physio-chemical & bacteriological properties of water. This laboratory involves the concepts of water supply, pollution control, recycling, waste (solid & liquid) disposal, radiation protection, industrial hygiene, environmental sustainability and public health.

It will be useful to suggest the type of treatment required and amount of dosage required for the treatment of water. It is also used to measure the required parameters of water and to check whether they are in accordance with the specified standards. Hence the suitability of water for different construction purposes can be determined in this laboratory. The quality check of water also plays an important role in water distribution and pollution control of water bodies.

The Department of Civil Engineering organized an “Awareness Session on mTutor”on 18/07/2026 from 11.00 a.m. to 1.00 p.m. at Thomas Alva Edison Hall, Cambridge Block. The session was delivered by Mr. Ramachandran Shenbagaraj, Vice President, Mobile Tutor Pvt. Ltd., Chennai.II year and III year B.E. Civil Engineering students attended the program.

The program aimed to introduce participants to the mTutor digital learning platform and its key features. ### Health Hacks for the Hustle on 24-09-2025

- September 25, 2025

The Women Empowerment Cell (WEC) of AAA College of Engineering and Technology organized an Health Awareness Program titled “Health Hacks for the Hustle” on 24.09.2025 from 3pm to 4.30pm at Thomas Alva Edison Hall, Cambridge Block, AAACET. The session was handled by Dr N.Ezhil, Assistant professor,Medical College, and Founder & Consultant of Ezhil Hospital, Virudhunagar.

She delivered an insightful and inspiring talk on mental health awareness, preventive measures for cancer, and the importance of early detection and regular health check-ups. She encouraged students to prioritize their well-being, maintain a balanced lifestyle, and seek timely medical advice. Dr. Ezhil shared practical tips for managing screen time and provided a Government toll-free helpline number for mental health support to help those struggling with digital addiction.

The programme was organized by Mrs.Jasmine Jayakodi,AP/CIVIL, and Mrs.Lalitha Tharani,AP/CSE with the support of Dr.N.Thenmoezhi, AP(SG)/ECE and all Women Empowerment Cell members.

The district chief educational officer of Virudhunagar, inaugurated the School Innovation programme for School science teachers to promote innovation from school level. More than 160 school teachers from Virudhunagar district participated. Dr Sekar, principal felicitated the gathering and distributed the certificates.

### SWATCHHATA HI SEVA CAMPAIGN on 28-09-2024

- November 14, 2024

In adherence to the circular (Letter No. F.No.2-68/RD/2021-22) issued by the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, the NSS Unit of AAACET successfully organized a comprehensive Cleanliness Awareness Campaign at the Government Hospital, Sivakasi on September 28, 2024. The primary objective of this initiative was to promote hygiene and cleanliness within and around the hospital premises and to educate the public on the detrimental effects of plastic usage, thereby fostering a cleaner and healthier environment for all. NSS volunteers cleaned the hospital and its surroundings, collecting plastic, paper, and other debris. All collected waste was meticulously segregated and then responsibly handed over to the Solid Waste Management Department. A highlight of the campaign was an impactful awareness skit performed by the NSS volunteers within the hospital premises. The skit vividly depicted the severe environmental and health impacts of plastic usage, particularly in public spaces like hospitals. The event not only resulted in a cleaner hospital environment but also effectively raised public awareness regarding cleanliness and sustainable waste management practices. The program was coordinated by NSS Coordinator Mr.S.Balamurugan and the Rotaract Club Coordinator Dr.R.Meby Selvaraj.

Sanjay Guru of I year AI & DS got III prize. B. Sobana, Shakthyananthi U A & R. Kavin Murugesan of I year AI & DS, C. Kavi Bala & K. S. Afreen Fathima of I year. CSE ‘A’, V. Vaishalini, C. Mahithasri & S. Nashrin Nisha of I year CSE ‘B’, R. Maheswaran of I year Mech, R. Rajalakshmi of II year CSE, S. Monika Sri of II year ECE got consolation prizes. The Management, Principal and Faculty Members congratulated the winners.

- Events college , NSS , Uncategorized

- November 5, 2023

In view of Vigilance Awareness Week 2023, the NSS Unit of AAA College of Engineering and Technology, in association with the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Department, Virudhunagar, organized the awareness program with the theme “Say No to Corruption, Commit to Nation” on November 1, 2023. This program aimed to raise awareness about the importance of vigilance, the consequences of corruption, and the role students play in maintaining a corruption-free society. The event was graced by the presence of our esteemed Chief Guest, Dr. M. Sekar, Principal, Mr.Salvan Durai, Inspector of Police, and Mr. Boominadhan, Inspector of Police, Virudhunagar, whose insights and experiences added great value to the program. The session included discussions on real-life case studies and the impact of corruption on society. A significant part of the program involved students taking a pledge to uphold ethical values, reject corruption, and report any unethical practices they might encounter. This program was coordinated by NSS Unit Coordinator, Mr. S. Balamurugan.

text:
### WORKSHOP ON INTERNET OF THINGS on 23-02-2023

Center for IIoT, AAACET conducted one day workshop on “Internet of Things” for the students from Arasan Ganesan Polytechnic College, Sivakasi on 2.02.2023. Mr. M. S. Kalyana Sundaram, AP/ EEE was the resource person for this programme. The workshop covered the basic concept of Internet of Things and the IoT based projects are discussed. as an example, smart home applications, smart city projects are elaborated in this workshop. Hands on session is also provided to the participants where they have worked with the Node MCU controllers and developed sensors based IOT projects. Total of 55 participants actively participated in this workshop and benefitted.

### World Radio Day Celebration on 13-02-2024

- February 23, 2024

The Department of Electronics Communication, AAA College of Engineering and Technology Sivakasi celebrated the World Radio Day on 13-02-2024 Tuesday. The day was proclaimed by the UNESCO in 2011 and observed annually to commemorate the anniversary of the first radio broadcast on February 13, 1922, by the United Nations (UN) Radio. The objective of World Radio Day is to raise greater awareness among the public and media regarding the importance of radio. The theme for the World Radio Day 2024 is “Radio: A century informing, entertaining and educating”. The United Nations states, “The 2024 observance highlights the history of radio and its powerful impact on news, drama, music and sports. As a part of this programme, a exhibition session of the radio receivers for understanding the evolution of radio receivers and guest lecture are arranged by the ECE department.

AAACET Principal Dr.M.Sekar inaugurated the exhibition of Vintage radio receivers arranged in the room no: 2101 ((Cambridge block I floor). In his inaugural speech, he recounted how radio service was a major source of national and international news for the general public before television, computers, internet and mobile phones were introduced. Dr. G. Jayahari Prabhu, AP/ECE, gave a briefing of his 1930s-era radio receiver collection with license note book used in 1970s for keeping the radio receivers. In his collections, greater number of radio receivers’ use valves i.e. vacuum tubes as active devices for detection, amplification, and other functions. Dr. T. Senthil, HOD/ECE, gave a presentation in which he discussed the history of radio receivers, beginning with Guglielmo Marconi, Lee De Forest—dubbed the father of radio—and Armstrong, who made groundbreaking contributions to the realm of wireless networks. The students and faculty members of the various departments of the AAACET participated in the exhibition and interacted with the organizers, regarding the early detectors, TRF and heterodyne receivers.

### Centre for Virtual Instrumentation (LabVIEW)

(LabVIEW)

#### Centre for Virtual Instrumentation

A Centre for Virtual Instrumentation focuses on promoting the best practices, advanced skills, and innovation within the LabVIEW environment. Laboratory Virtual Instrument Engineering Workbench (LabVIEW) is a system design software platform developed by National Instruments, used for data acquisition, instrument control, automation, and industrial systems. LabVIEW is a graphical programming environment that provides unique productivity accelerators for test system development, such as an intuitive approach to programming, connectivity to any instrument, and fully integrated user interfaces. An efficient LabVIEW application is designed without unnecessary operations, with minimal occupation including code, data, block diagram, front panel, and GUI updates.

#### Features

- It has a user-friendly drag-and-drop kind of interactive User Interface.

- It supports thousands of inbuilt functions that range from analysis and I/O etc. These belong to the function palette

- LabVIEW has a modular design making. So it is easy to scale and modular programs.

- It has a plethora of professional development tools that help integrate and debug large applications.

- It has the tools needed for many open environment developments.

- It supports object-oriented programming structures enabling encapsulation and inheritance to create modular and extensible code.

- Being a compiled language it is faster.

### CENTRE OF EXCELLENCE IN PROJECT MANAGEMENT

The Centre of Excellence is equipped with PRIMAVERA software which is extensively used for project management.

#### CENTRE OF EXCELLENCE IN PROJECT MANAGEMENT

Centre of Excellence in project management was established in AAACET in the year 2018. Centre of Excellence is equipped with PRIMAVERA software which is extensively used for project management. Primavera is an enterprise project portfolio management software. It includes project management, scheduling, risk analysis, opportunity management, resource management, collaboration and control capabilities, and integrates with other enterprise software such as Oracle and SAP’s ERP systems.

It is used in the Engineering, Construction, Aerospace, Defense, Utilities and Oil & Gas industries. In addition, it is the tool of choice for power users, such as schedulers and project managers, in industries where detailed, fast, accurate scheduling and the critical path method are crucial to the planning, execution and success of a project. The knowledge gained in the lab eventually equips the students to provide quality service once employed in the industry.

#### Objectives

- To present an overview of PRIMAVERA and describe its application in different fields.

- To enable students to understand the execution of the projects and track its progress.

- To act as a bridge between student community and the construction industry in creating the knowledge on quality project delivery.

- To enhance the students’ employability and to create entrepreneurs exploiting PRIMAVERA course.

- To provide practical and hands-on training on PRIMAVERA.

- To organize workshops and certificate courses.

##### Co-ordinator

Dr.M.Karthiga, Assistant Professor, Department of Civil Engineering

### Few clicks of SONYFEST ’17 ....more coming soon!!

Moving upwards in age, SONYFEST megaevent steps into the fifth year of cultural celebrations. SONYFEST platform is fashioned to identify the amateur artists and bring to light their artifacts. This platform has shaped a number of talented artists and is still surprised with new and young artists coming up every year. The first week of the fest is crammed with off stage events, starting with Language Focused Events: Elocution, Creative Writing and Star Wars are a few to mention.The second week kicks off with a new gallery of events when things become more interesting. The fun continues watching the participation in Vegetable Carving, Rangoli, Dumscharade and ADZAP. Vegetables and Fruits add beauty to humans. It is a fun to reverse this psychology and the students go crazy adding beauty to fruits and vegetables by carving designs. Colours are the reflection of nature and they rejuvenate our minds. There is a spectacular display of colours on the day of Rangoli Competition. Flowers and lights add life to the colours of the Rangoli. “Heard melodies are sweet, but those unheard are sweeter” – John Keats. Our students proved that it is not only sweeter but also funnier to comprehend the secret codes in Dumbcharade. Lights, Camera, Action and at the click of every board in ADZAP, there is a new Advertising Director promoting a brand new product. An array of advertisements entertained the audience. Sonyfest opens the doors for its hugely popular and delicious competition “Cooking” at the end of the fortnight. With the overwhelming participants, there is a tough competition for the recreational cooks. Flavored and mouth-watering vegetarian dishes are prepared by them. There is a feast to the taste buds of the professional cook-cum-judges. The extremely enthusiastic show for the audience is the Dance. Dance with delightful music is a wonderful expression of the hidden language of the soul. The audiences cheer as the dancers dance to the tune. Next on the row is a professional task – Best Manager – which aims at developing every aspect of experience and exposure needed by the students to manage situations in the work environment.

### SAE Trekking & Auto Expo Visit on 30.09.2023

- October 4, 2023

SAE Trek is a one-day event that focuses on Automotive Knowledge competition by objective exam and dream car sketching contest. The Trek mainly emphasizes the need and positive effects of relaxation, joy and fun apart from getting to know new friends. So, trek were conducted on various factors like safety, pleasant weather, greenery, etc

Trek started at around 9 a.m from Madurai. Mr. A. Vignesh Moorthy Pandian accompanied it for the trek. Trek started from Alagarkoil hills down site, with a total strength of around 15 members. We trekked uphill towards Alagarkoil Hills, taking pictures on the way and enjoying the lush green around us. At around 11:00 a.m. we reached Pazhamudhircholai, had a small break there and started back downhill through the forest side. This was wonderful as we could come by watching the nature and enjoy the scenery around us.

After that, we visited Madurai Auto Expo 2023, at the Tamukkam Ground in Madurai. The expo aimed to show cases the latest developments and changes in the automobile industry, particularly in cars, two-wheelers, Lorries, tractors, and spare parts. With 140 stalls in total, including 20 stalls for cars and two-wheelers, this event brought together leading auto parts manufacturing plants and manufacturers from across India. The expo provided a platform to understand and appreciate the recent advancements in the automotive industry, with a specific focus on spare parts. Notably, the inclusion of pre-1947 vehicles, vintage bikes, and cars added a unique historical perspective to the event, giving visitors the chance to witness the evolution of automobiles. The event aimed to raise awareness about road safety and accident prevention, which is a critical concern in the automotive industry

The programme was well organised by our Secretary Dr.P.Karvannan., Correspondent Dr.P.Ganesan., Joint Secretary Dr.K.Vignesh Kumar., Principal Dr.M.Sekar, Dr.R.Selvabharathi, HOD / Mech and the Event co-ordinator Mr. A. Name of the Lab: Lab Technician | Concrete & Highway Engineering Laboratory: Mr. A. Kamal, D.M.E.,

- CE3412 – Materials Testing Laboratory (II year – IV Semester)

Concrete is one of the important construction materials. Study of its constituents and their properties is essential for preparing desired mix so as to develop required strength necessary for various types of Structures. The durability of the structures depends upon the care with which ingredients of concrete are selected, mixed, placed, compacted and cured. Concrete is used not only for construction of building, but also for concrete roads, gravity dams, retaining walls, water tanks, airport runway pavements, etc.

The information regarding various properties of concrete in its plastic stage as well as hardened Stage is necessary to enable the engineer for quality control during construction work. Knowledge of the subject is essential for the Design of Concrete Structures. Strength, workability, durability are important characteristics of concrete. Compressive strength of concrete describes the load caring capacity, workability is the indicator of ease with which we work on concrete, whereas durability shows the resistance of concrete to environmental attack.

All these properties of concrete are determined by performing the experiments in Concrete & Highway Engineering Laboratory. Also, the students will able to design various grades of concrete by DOE, ACI and Indian method of concrete mix design. In addition, the properties of construction materials used in highway engineering are also determined in this laboratory.

In Computer Science, a data structure is a data organization, management and storage format that enable efficient access and modification. More precisely, a data structure is a collection of data values, the relationships among them, and the functions or operations that can be applied to the data. Data structures provide a means to manage large amounts of data efficiently for uses such as large internet indexing services. Usually, efficient data structures are key to designing efficient algorithms. Different kinds of data structures are suited to different kinds of applications, and some are highly specialized to specific tasks. Some formal design methods and programming languages emphasize data structures, rather than algorithms, as the key organizing factor in software design. Data structures can be used to organize the storage and retrieval of information stored in both main memory and secondary memory.

The Department of Computer Science and Engineering has a well-established Programming and Data Structures Laboratory. The laboratory is supported by Data centre and all computers in this laboratory are connected to the Data centre via LAN.

### Alumni Induction Day and Farewell on 29-04-2024

- April 18, 2024

AAACET alumni association cordially invite you all for the Alumni Induction Day and Farewell on 29.04.2024.

### IT Association Inauguration on 03-07-2026

- July 8, 2026

The Department of Information Technology successfully organized its Association Inauguration Function on Friday, 3 July 2026, with the objective of encouraging students to explore the latest developments in the field of Information Technology and to strengthen the connection between academic learning and industry practices. The event marked the beginning of the department’s academic association activities for the year and provided an excellent platform for students to gain knowledge from eminent academicians and industry experts. The inauguration was attended by faculty members, students, and distinguished guests, making it a memorable and intellectually enriching occasion.

The function was graced by two eminent chief guests, Dr. R. Anandha Murugan, Founder of Purvidy, India & Dubai, and Dr. C. P. Sabariram, Assistant Professor, V.O.C. College of Engineering, Thoothukudi. Both speakers shared their expertise and practical experiences, providing students with valuable insights into the rapidly evolving technological landscape. Their addresses emphasized the importance of continuous learning, innovation, research, and skill development to succeed in today’s competitive IT industry.

The seminar focused on the emerging technologies of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Computer Vision, and Enterprise Cloud Platforms, which are transforming industries across the globe. The speakers explained how these technologies have become the foundation of modern industrial automation by enabling organizations to process large volumes of visual and digital data efficiently. Students learned that Artificial Intelligence has evolved beyond automation to become a powerful decision-making tool capable of recognizing patterns, making predictions, and supporting intelligent business operations. They also understood how Computer Vision enables machines to interpret and analyze images and videos in a manner similar to human vision, thereby supporting applications across manufacturing, healthcare, transportation, agriculture, retail, and security.

The resource persons elaborated on the role of Enterprise Cloud Platforms in supporting AI-driven applications. They explained that cloud computing provides highly scalable infrastructure capable of processing enormous volumes of data while offering flexibility, security, and cost efficiency. By integrating AI with cloud platforms, organizations can analyze visual information in real time and transform unstructured data into meaningful business insights. This integration enables enterprises to improve productivity, optimize operations, and make informed decisions based on accurate and timely information.

Students were introduced to several practical applications of AI-powered Computer Vision systems used in industries. One of the major applications discussed was automated data capture, where cloud-hosted Optical Character Recognition (OCR) technology extracts information from invoices, receipts, identity documents, and various business records. This process significantly reduces manual effort, improves data accuracy, and accelerates business workflows.

### IT Association Inauguration on 03-07-2026

Students were introduced to several practical applications of AI-powered Computer Vision systems used in industries. One of the major applications discussed was automated data capture, where cloud-hosted Optical Character Recognition (OCR) technology extracts information from invoices, receipts, identity documents, and various business records. This process significantly reduces manual effort, improves data accuracy, and accelerates business workflows.

Another important application was quality assurance in manufacturing industries, where AI-enabled vision systems inspect products on assembly lines and identify microscopic defects that are difficult for the human eye to detect. Such intelligent inspection systems improve product quality, minimize production errors, and reduce operational costs.

The seminar also highlighted workplace safety monitoring as an important application of Computer Vision. Students learned how AI-powered surveillance systems continuously monitor industrial environments to ensure that employees comply with safety regulations by wearing appropriate protective equipment and to identify hazardous situations before accidents occur. These systems contribute to creating safer workplaces while reducing risks and enhancing organizational compliance. In addition, the speakers explained how operational intelligence is achieved by analyzing camera feeds to monitor customer movement, understand consumer behavior, optimize store layouts, and improve asset utilization. Such intelligent analytics help organizations make data-driven decisions that enhance operational efficiency and customer satisfaction.

A significant part of the session focused on the architecture of deploying AI-based Computer Vision systems in enterprises. The speakers explained the differences between centralized cloud AI and hybrid edge AI approaches. In the centralized cloud architecture, computationally intensive tasks such as deep learning model training and retraining are performed using powerful cloud computing resources.

Data collected from multiple business locations is aggregated into centralized repositories, enabling organizations to build highly accurate AI models. Although cloud computing offers excellent scalability and centralized management, transmitting high-definition video streams continuously to cloud servers can increase bandwidth usage and operational costs.

The concept of hybrid edge AI was presented as an efficient solution for addressing latency, privacy, and bandwidth challenges. Students learned that lightweight AI models can be deployed directly on edge devices such as smart cameras, embedded systems, and gateway devices, allowing data to be processed locally with minimal delay.

This enables immediate detection of events and real-time alerts, which are essential in applications such as industrial automation, surveillance, and autonomous systems. Since sensitive data remains within the organization’s local infrastructure, hybrid edge AI also enhances privacy and regulatory compliance. The enterprise cloud continues to function as a centralized management platform by securely distributing software updates and optimized AI models to edge devices, thereby combining the strengths of both cloud and edge computing.

### IT Association Inauguration on 03-07-2026

Since sensitive data remains within the organization’s local infrastructure, hybrid edge AI also enhances privacy and regulatory compliance. The enterprise cloud continues to function as a centralized management platform by securely distributing software updates and optimized AI models to edge devices, thereby combining the strengths of both cloud and edge computing.

Throughout the seminar, the speakers emphasized the growing demand for professionals with expertise in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Computer Vision, Cloud Computing, and Data Analytics. They encouraged students to strengthen their programming skills, participate in research activities, undertake industry-oriented projects, and pursue professional certifications to remain competitive in the evolving technology sector. They also highlighted the importance of interdisciplinary learning, ethical AI practices, and continuous innovation in addressing real-world challenges.

The interactive session at the end of the programme provided students with an opportunity to clarify their doubts regarding career opportunities, research directions, industrial applications, and emerging trends in AI and cloud technologies.

The discussions inspired students to explore advanced technologies with greater enthusiasm and confidence. The Association Inauguration Function concluded successfully with positive feedback from participants, leaving students motivated to enhance their technical knowledge, develop practical skills, and prepare themselves for successful careers in the rapidly advancing field of Information Technology.

### One Day Workshop & Hands on Training on CNC Router on 20-06-2026

- June 22, 2026

Name of the Event | One Day Workshop & Hands on Training on CNC Router
Date of the Event | 20 th June 2026
Venue | CAM Laboratory, Cambridge Block
Title | One Day Workshop & Hands on Training on CNC Router
Chief Guest | Mr.G.Sastha Roopan, CEO at SR 3D Solutions, Sivakasi
Total Participants: | 46 Students
Beneficiaries | College Students and Staff
Description about the Programme | The Department of Mechanical Engineering, in association with the International Association of Engineers (IAENG), organized a one-day workshop and hands-on training program on CNC router operations for final-year students on June 20, 2026, featuring resource person Mr.G.Sastha Roopan, CEO at SR 3D Solutions, Sivakasi. The technical session provided students with end-to-end practical exposure to subtractive manufacturing, beginning with assembling and installing a CNC router from scratch to understand its mechanical and electronic framework. Participants learned to convert 2D raster images into vector formats, program toolpaths using OpenBuilds CAM software, and write foundational G-code. A core focus was placed on precision machine setup, where students mastered work coordinate offsets to establish workpiece origins and tool length offset methods to ensure accurate cutting depths. The workshop concluded with a live, hands-on session where students secured raw materials, applied offset parameters, and operated the CNC router under expert supervision to fabricate finished components. The program was coordinated by Mr.S.Balamurugan, Assistant Professor, Mechanical Engineering.
