### KAAVAL UTHAVI APP – AWARENESS PROGRAM – 13-03-2025

- March 15, 2025

On 13-03-2025, the NSS unit of AAACET, in collaboration with the Anti-Human Trafficking Unit of Virudhunagar, conducted a comprehensive awareness program focusing on the critical utility of the ‘Kaaval Uthavi’ mobile application. The program was graced by the presence of esteemed Chief Guests, Mr.C.Kannan, Special Sub-inspector of Police, and Mr.R.Parthiban, Special Sub-inspector of Police. They delivered an informative session detailing the various functionalities of the app, emphasizing its role as a vital tool for ensuring personal safety. In addition to app awareness, the session also included an important discussion on Ragging prevention. The officials emphasized the consequences of ragging and the impact it has on victims. Students were encouraged to stand against any form of harassment and utilize the Kaaval Uthavi app to report such incidents promptly. They highlighted the app’s ability to facilitate swift communication with law enforcement during critical situations, thereby enabling rapid response and intervention. To provide a practical understanding of the app’s operation, a live demonstration was conducted with active student participation. Students volunteered to simulate emergency scenarios, triggering the app’s alert system. They were able to experience first-hand the prompt response received from the officials, including immediate phone calls, after utilizing the app’s emergency features. This hands-on experience significantly enhanced the students’ understanding of the app’s effectiveness and reliability. The event underscored the importance of leveraging technology for public safety and empowering individuals with the tools necessary to protect themselves during emergencies.

- EC 8681 – Microprocessor and Microcontroller Laboratory (III Year – VI Semester)

The main objective of the Microprocessor and Microcontroller lab facility is to enable the students to gain practical knowledge about various types of microprocessors and microcontrollers and to develop their own programs and implement the same in microprocessors/microcontrollers for various applications in electronic and communication engineering. Various types of arithmetic and logical operations are taught to the students in the laboratory so that it will enable them to understand the concepts about assembly language programming, CPU, memory and I/O design, interfacing of programmable chips and peripherals such as stepper motors, analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog converters, etc.

Various types of microprocessor, microcontroller trainer kits and interfacing modules are available in this lab. These are used to provide intensive practical exposure to the students in understanding the internal architecture of the microprocessors/microcontrollers and in developing the associated software and hardware for various applications.

The students are trained to understand the Serial Data Communication using microprocessor/microcontrollers trainer kits, to interface the microprocessor with different circuits such as A/D converter, Stepper motors, DC mototrs, LCD and Seven Segment displays, etc.

page_title: Faculty Development Programme on Internet of Things
text:
### Faculty Development Programme on Internet of Things

- January 9, 2019

Centre for Industry oriented Internet of Things organizes Two days Faculty Development Programme on Internet of Things on 16/01/2019 & 17/01/2019 in association with Riyasaa Labs.

The Internet of things (IoT) is the network of physical devices, vehicles, home appliances and other items embedded with electronics, software, sensors, actuators, and network connectivity which enable these objects to connect and exchange data. IoT platform provides development of number of applications smart grids, virtual power plants, smart homes, intelligent transportation and smart cities. This FDP aims to make the participants realize the importance of IoT and its applications in various fields as well as to demonstrate some demo projects on specific applications. It gives an introduction to IoT, so that participants can learn to build their own IoT products for various applications, and it also enables them to convert their product ideas into a working prototype.

### Industrial Visit – Technexus Association on 07-02-2026

- February 11, 2026

An industrial visit was successfully conducted by Technexus Students’ Technical Association on 7th February 2026 (Saturday) at 11:00 AM at Floor I, Spectrum IT Park, located on Mahakavi G Road, Ernakulam South, Kochi, Kerala. The primary objective of this visit was to bridge the gap between academic learning and real-time industry practices by exposing students to current technologies and professional working environments in the IT sector.

The visit commenced with a formal welcome by the company’s HR Divya N representative and the speaker who introduced herself and provided a detailed overview of the organization. She explained the company’s vision, mission, areas of expertise, and overall work culture. The introduction also highlighted the importance of teamwork, continuous learning, and adaptability in the IT industry.

This session helped students understand how corporate environments function and the expectations placed on engineers in real-world projects.

Following the introductory session, an extensive technical session was conducted focusing on DevOps concepts, which were explained in a structured, step-by-step manner. The speaker began with GitHub, emphasizing its role in version control and collaborative development. She explained how multiple developers work on a single project using repositories, branches, commits, and pull requests. This was followed by a clear explanation of servers and local servers, where the difference between local development environments and remote production servers was discussed in detail.

The session then moved on to scripting concepts and languages, highlighting the importance of automation in DevOps. The speaker explained how scripting languages such as Shell scripting and Python are used to automate repetitive tasks, manage servers, and streamline deployment processes. Students were able to understand how scripting forms the backbone of efficient DevOps operations.

Next, the speaker introduced build tools and plugins, with special focus on Maven. She explained the Maven build lifecycle, dependency management, and the role of plugins in automating tasks such as compiling, testing, packaging, and deploying applications. Real- time examples were shared to show how Maven is used in continuous integration environments.The concept of containerization was then explained using Docker, where the speaker described how applications are packaged with all their dependencies to ensure consistency across different environments. This was followed by a detailed explanation of Kubernetes, focusing on container orchestration, scaling, load balancing, and fault tolerance in large-scale applications.

### Industrial Visit – Technexus Association on 07-02-2026

Real- time examples were shared to show how Maven is used in continuous integration environments.The concept of containerization was then explained using Docker, where the speaker described how applications are packaged with all their dependencies to ensure consistency across different environments. This was followed by a detailed explanation of Kubernetes, focusing on container orchestration, scaling, load balancing, and fault tolerance in large-scale applications.

A significant portion of the session was dedicated to explaining CI/CD pipelines. The speaker walked students through each stage of the pipeline, from code commit and automated testing to build, deployment, and monitoring. She emphasized how CI/CD improves software quality, reduces manual errors, and accelerates the delivery process.In addition to technical tools, the speaker explained software development methodologies, particularly Agile and Waterfall. She clearly compared both methodologies, explaining their workflows, advantages, limitations, and use cases. The Agile methodology was explained in detail, including concepts such as sprints, continuous feedback, and iterative development, highlighting its relevance in modern DevOps-driven projects.

The session was highly interactive, and students were encouraged to ask questions throughout. The speaker patiently addressed all queries, clarified doubts, and provided career guidance related to DevOps roles, required skill sets, and industry expectations. The practical approach and real-world examples used during the session greatly enhanced student understanding.

Overall, the industrial visit proved to be an enriching and educational experience. It provided students with in-depth knowledge of DevOps tools, development methodologies, and real-time industry workflows. The initiative by Technexus Students’ Technical Association was highly successful and played a vital role in motivating students to develop industry-relevant technical skills and prepare themselves for future professional challenges.

### Cloud Bridge Foundation from 05-01-2026 to 09-01-2026

- January 10, 2026

The Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering , AAA College of Engineering and Technology, Sivakasi , in association with iTech Academy , jointly organized a Five Days Certificate Course on “Cloud Bridge Foundation” for the IV Year EEE students . The program was conducted from 5th January 2026 to 9th January 2026 at Thomas Alva Edison Seminar Hall, Cambridge Block , with the objective of providing fundamental knowledge and practical exposure to cloud computing technologies.

The primary aim of the program was to equip students with a strong foundation in cloud computing architecture, operating systems, networking essentials, cloud services, and cloud security concepts , thereby preparing them for entry-level cloud roles and industry-oriented skill development. The course was meticulously planned to ensure a balance between theoretical concepts and hands-on practical sessions.

The sessions were handled by Mr. Radhakrishnan , an experienced Entrepreneur and Industry Expert in Security Surveillance and Cloud Technologies , who has over 14 years of professional experience in system implementation, infrastructure management, and training. He has significantly contributed to various Tamil Nadu Government sectors , including CCTNS (Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and Systems) and TNSTC Corporation , and has extensive experience in mentoring students and professionals. His industry exposure and practical approach greatly enhanced the quality and effectiveness of the training program.

The training sessions were conducted daily with structured modules covering computer fundamentals, operating systems, networking essentials, cloud computing concepts, AWS services, cloud security, and virtual private cloud (VPC) implementation . Students were introduced to core concepts such as hardware components, memory systems, operating systems, IP addressing, LAN implementation, cloud service models, Amazon EC2, AWS IAM, and VPC configuration . Each session included demonstrations, lab activities, quizzes, and assessments , ensuring active participation and continuous evaluation.

Special emphasis was given to practical learning , where students gained hands-on experience through Amazon EC2 instance creation, IAM user configuration, VPC setup, and launching web servers in a cloud environment . These sessions enabled students to understand real-world cloud deployment scenarios and security practices followed in the industry.

The program also incorporated daily quizzes and a final assessment , which helped in monitoring the progress of the participants and reinforcing their understanding of the concepts taught. The students actively participated throughout the program and displayed great enthusiasm in learning modern cloud technologies.

On successful completion of the course, all participants were awarded certificates from iTech Academy , adding value to their academic and professional portfolio. The program was well-received by the students and proved to be highly beneficial in enhancing their technical competency and industry readiness.

page_title: Hands on Practice on Internet of Things Using Arduino
text:
### Hands on Practice on Internet of Things Using Arduino

- June 29, 2019

Three days value added course on “Hands on Practice on Internet of Things” was held during 17-06-2019 to 19-06-2019 at Centre for IIoT, AAA College of Engineering and Technology. 38 final year students of Electronics and Communication Engineering were participated. This course made the students to realize the importance of IoT and its applications in various fields. This training was imparted in different applications of wireless, embedded and IoT using lecture sessions, hands on training and developing product ideas into a working prototype.

The course started with a formal inauguration ceremony. Dr.A.Shenbagarajan, Associate Professor/CSE delivered the origin and importance of IoT followed by the recent development of IoT. He gave talk on basics of sensors and actuators, Arduino programming – Interfacing and configuration of sensors with Arduino software. Dr.A.Shenbagarajan, Associate Professor/CSE, Mrs.K.Padmapriya, Assistant Professor/ECE and Mr.M.S.Kalyanasundaram, Assistant Professor/EEE handled hands on training on working with sensors like Temperature, Humidity, IR Sensor, Ultrasonic Sensor, Gas Sensor, Light and Moisture Sensor, PIR and Colour Sensors, HC-05 Bluetooth module by controlling the sensors and actuators using HC-05 module Bluetooth mobile app. By using this concept, students designed a smart home system of controlling the light and fan using mobile app. Node MCU – ESP8266 and integrating the sensor real time values to the cloud. The sensed data is uploaded to the ThingsSpeak cloud using ESP8266 Module. The real time data is visualized as graphical representation using matlab code available in the cloud. Dr.S.Sevugarajan, Professor & Head/ECE handled hands on voice controlled using Bluetooth, and Home Automation using Bit Voicer.

### Advanced Data Structures and Algorithms Laboratory

Name of the Lab | Advanced Data Structures and Algorithms Laboratory
Year of Establishment | 2025
Venue | Cambridge Block
Room No. | 2334
Area | 83.61 Sq.m
Faculty In-charge | Mrs.E.SELVAMANJU, AP/CSE
Lab Technician | Ms.K.Malathi

An Advanced Data Structures and Algorithms Laboratory is a specialized facility designed to strengthen students’ problem-solving and computational thinking abilities through the practical implementation of efficient data structures and algorithmic techniques. The lab provides an environment where students can analyze and compare different algorithms, explore their performance, and understand how complexity impacts real-world applications.

Advanced Data Structures and Algorithms play a significant role in the foundation of computer science, supporting the design of optimized solutions for modern computing challenges. In today’s demand for high-performance systems, selecting the right data structure and algorithm ensures efficiency, scalability, and reliability. This laboratory equips students with hands-on experience in implementing abstract data types, tree and graph structures, hashing techniques, dynamic programming, greedy strategies, searching and sorting algorithms, as well as advanced topics such as pattern matching and network flow.

The laboratory is supported with modern computational facilities, development platforms, and programming environments such as GCC, CodeBlocks, Eclipse, and Linux terminals. Students perform experiments that include designing and evaluating algorithms, measuring time and space complexities, and understanding trade-offs between different approaches while solving real-time computational problems.

The lab is well equipped with high-performance systems, stable internet connectivity, and an air-conditioned environment with power backup support to ensure uninterrupted learning. All systems are networked through a secure LAN and supported by the institutional data center for centralized access and easy resource sharing.

The primary objective of this laboratory is to develop students’ analytical and logical reasoning skills by enabling them to design efficient solutions for challenging problems. Through practice-oriented sessions involving implementation, testing, and optimization, students gain the ability to choose appropriate data structures, evaluate algorithmic efficiency, and build robust programs. This laboratory serves as a strong foundation for advanced computing courses, competitive programming, and future research in algorithm design.

page_title: Dr. S. Sevuragan M.Tech (IISc) PhD (IISc) PDF(USA)
text:
### Dr. S. Sevuragan M.Tech (IISc) PhD (IISc) PDF(USA)

- August 3, 2018

Dr. S. Sevugarajan is currently heading the Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering and the Department of Science and Humanities at AAA College of Engineering and Technology. He obtained his Bachelor’s degree in 1995 with Physics as a major subject and completed his Master’s degree in the field of material Science in 1997 at Anna University. In 1997 he joined Indian Institute of Science (IISc) at Bangalore and obtained an additional research master’s degree (MSc[Engg]) in Instrumentation Engineering. After completion of his master’s degree at IISc in 1999, he continued his research work at IISc and obtained his PhD degree in 2005. Immediately after completing his PhD, he was invited to U.S.A to work as a post-doctoral fellow with Dr. Clemmer at Indiana University, USA. His post-Doctoral work was based on split-field drift tube/ion mobility mass spectrometry (IM-MS). In 2006 he joined Vanderbilt University, USA as a research associate. At Vanderbilt University he 1. Designed and developed a Dual-Source Electrospray/MALDI Ion Mobility-Mass Spectrometer (IM-MS) for Biomolecular Structural Characterization. 2. Designed and developed the single and 8-channel ESI source, Drift tube, ion Extraction source and vacuum chambers and their associated electronics and RF power source for IM-MS. 3. Designed and developed “A novel multiplexed data acquisition technique that utilizes fast repetition MALDI ionization source to enhance the sensitivity of IM-MS”. During his stay at Vanderbilt University he has also completed a consultancy project in designing the mechanical and Instrumentation setup for ESI Source for Accelerated Mass Spectrometer in Prof. Tannenbaum’ s laboratory, MIT, Boston, MA, USA

In 2013 he joined Acharya Institute of Technology as a professor in Electronics and Communication Engineering department. During 2015 he was invited to Florida International University, USA, as a visiting faculty where he worked on the Design and Development of Voice based Greetings/Control System for Tele-Presence Robot (TELEBOT).

He has supervised several masters and undergraduate students. He has published over 30 peer-reviewed research papers in reputed research Journals having very high Impact factors (~15) and book chapters.Dr. S. Sevugarajanis an active member of IEEE. He is a highly energetic, dynamic and self-motivated person. Apart from Academics, he has been contributing lots in Intellectual Property Rights Cell (IP Cell). He has organized several workshops and conferences at both national and international levels.

His research interests include: Design and development of Telepresence Robots, automated unmanned aerial vehicles, Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning techniques for Agriculture and Health care systems and in the design and development of Ion-Mobilty Mass Spectormeters,

page_title: Hands-on training on web security testing on 24-01-2025
text:
### Hands-on training on web security testing on 24-01-2025

- January 29, 2026

The Department of Computer Science and Engineering (Cyber Security), AAA College of Engineering and Technology, in association with CRYPTNOVA, successfully organized a Hands-On Training on “Web Security Testing” on Saturday, 24th January 2026, at 9:30 A.M. in the Cyber Tech Centre Laboratory, Cambridge Block.

The programme commenced with a welcome address by a student representative from the Department of CSE (Cyber Security), who warmly welcomed the Chief Guest, faculty members, and students, and briefly outlined the objective of the hands-on training programme.

This was followed by the Presidential Address delivered by Dr. P. Elamparithi, Associate Professor and Head of the Department, CSE (Cyber Security). In his address, he emphasized the importance of hands-on learning, industry exposure, and practical skill development in the field of cyber security, and encouraged students to actively participate and make the best use of the training session.

The introduction of the Chief Guest was given by a student representative, who highlighted the academic background, professional achievements, and industry experience of the resource person.

The hands-on training session was conducted by Mr. E. Guru Chandran, B.E., Software Developer & Security DRI, Zoho Corporation Pvt. Ltd., Tenkasi, a proud alumnus of AAA College of Engineering and Technology. The session focused on providing practical exposure to web application security, vulnerability assessment, and real-time web security testing techniques.

As part of the session, the resource person explained the fundamentals of server and client communication, including HTTP/HTTPS protocols, request–response mechanisms, cookies, sessions, and authentication workflows. This foundational knowledge helped students understand how web applications function and where security vulnerabilities commonly arise.

The training also included extensive hands-on practice using the Burp Suite tool, where students learned how to intercept and analyze web traffic, identify vulnerabilities such as SQL Injection, Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), and authentication flaws, and understand common attack vectors. Additionally, the resource person discussed preventive measures and secure coding practices to mitigate these attacks, emphasizing industry-recommended security controls and best practices.

The session was highly interactive, with students actively participating in hands-on activities and clarifying their doubts through discussions with the resource person. The training significantly enhanced students’ understanding of real-world web security challenges, attack handling, and defensive strategies used in the industry.

The programme concluded with a vote of thanks proposed by a student representative, who expressed sincere gratitude to the Chief Guest, management, Head of the Department, faculty members, coordinators, and students for their valuable support and active participation, which contributed to the successful completion of the programme.

### HANDS-ON WITH GITHUB FROM CLONE TO COMMIT on 07-02-2026

- February 9, 2026

The Department of Computer Science and Engineering (Cyber Security), AAA College of Engineering and Technology, in association with CRYPTNOVA , successfully organized a workshop titled Hands-on with GitHub “From Clone to Commit” on Friday, 07th February 2026 , at 9:30 A.M. in the Cyber Tech Centre Laboratory, Cambridge Block .

The programme commenced with a welcome address by Ms. Sandeepa Samayan S, III Year, Department of CSE (Cyber Security), who warmly welcomed the Chief Guest, management members, Head of the Department, faculty members, and students.

This was followed by a felicitation address by Dr. P. Elamparithi , Associate Professor and Head, Department of CSE (Cyber Security). In his address, he stressed the significance of hands-on learning, industry exposure, and continuous skill development in tools such as Git and GitHub, which play a vital role in collaborative and secure software development practices.

The introduction of the Chief Guest was given by Mr. Vijayakumar V , III year, who briefed the audience on the professional background, industry experience, and technical expertise of the resource person.

The technical session was handled by Mr. D. Samuel Rajan, B.E., DevOps Engineer, HandBuild Apps , who delivered an insightful and practical session on Git and GitHub workflows. The session began with an introduction to Git and its role in source code management, followed by a discussion on latest industry trends and current technology news relevant to software development and DevOps practices.

The resource person then covered Git basics and local repository operations , enabling students to understand initialization, staging, committing, and tracking changes effectively. He further explained Git branching and merging techniques , highlighting their importance in collaborative development and real-time project handling. A hands-on demonstration on pushing code to GitHub repositories was also provided, giving students practical exposure to remote repository management.

In addition, the session included guidance on industry-relevant courses and certifications , recommended technology news sources for continuous learning, and an overview of contributing to open-source projects , motivating students to actively participate in the developer community.

The session was highly interactive, with students actively engaging in hands-on activities and clarifying their doubts. The programme significantly enhanced the students’ understanding of real-world version control workflows and industry best practices.

The programme concluded with a vote of thanks proposed by Mr. Parthiban S , III Year, who expressed sincere gratitude to the Chief Guest, management, Head of the Department, faculty members, coordinators, and students for their support and participation in making the event a grand success.

page_title: Commencement Ceremony for the First Year Students – 02-09-2024
text:
### Commencement Ceremony for the First Year Students – 02-09-2024

AAA College of Engineering and Technology, Sivakasi the commencement ceremony for the first year students for the academic year 2024-2025 was held on Monday 02.09.2024. The event was presided over by Dr. Ganesan, Principal of the college and Mr. Amarnath, Trustee. Dr. Revathy Subbulakshmi, Bar Speaker, was present as the special guest.

First Year Head of Department Dr. Dharmaraja delivered the welcome address. College Principal Dr.M. Sekar in his inaugural address informed the students and parents about the regulations, syllabus and other details of the college. He also introduced all the professors working in the college to the students and parents. Congratulatory message was given by correspondent Dr. Ganesan who said that it is commendable that AAA College has got NBA and NAAC accreditations in 13 years of its establishment. He also said that the information that AAA College has been ranked 21st in the Anna University ranking list shows the hard work of the teachers and students of AAA College. Such a proud AAA college is working with the high aim of providing high quality technical education to all the students and requested the students to make proper use of it and progress in life.

As a part of the function, AAA college students who won first place in volleyball and chess competitions organized by Anna University were felicitated on the stage.

The special guest Mrs. Revathi Subbulakshmi in her keynote speech said: “The college we study is a place where we can determine our future and it is a place where we develop our management and personality. Students should always be happy and take advantage of the opportunity without any fear or hesitation. We have to renew ourselves daily. Everyone should act with the realization that time is like life.

Parents should accustom their children to simple lifestyles. Students should bring out their unique talents. Only teachers are the seeds of our progress and only they are happy in our growth.” The speech by the special guest was meant to inspire students and parents.

At the end of the ceremony, Professor. Tychicus of English department delivered the vote of thanks.

page_title: Entrepreneurship opportunities in HVAC sector on 25-11-2023
text:
### Entrepreneurship opportunities in HVAC sector on 25-11-2023

The Institution’s Innovation Council (IIC) and Entrepreneurship Development Cell (EDC), organized a One-day Workshop titled ‘Entrepreneurship opportunities in HVAC sector.’ The session took place on November 25, 2023, at 10.00 a.m.

Dr.R.Selvabharathi, HoD/MECH, presided over the event. The session commenced with a welcome address from Mr. M. Sivasankar, EDC Coordinator.

Mr.N.kannan, Proprietor, NK Enterprises, Virudhunagar, served as the resource person for the session. He initiated the session by highlighting his expertise and experience in the field of entrepreneurial opportunities in the HVAC sector. The speaker guided the students about recent trends in Refrigeration and Air Conditioning. He provides information regarding HVAC systems, heat exchangers, types of compressors and their working. Also, he elaborates heat load calculation by using thermal software (Thermals).

In the afternoon session, he explained fields of utilizations and also the consumption of energy by the systems. He stressed upon the global warming potential refrigerants and alternate long-time solutions. He guided the young minds to start using natural refrigerants in refrigeration and air conditioning systems to achieve greener and sustainable future. He ended the session with a thought-provoking note “Nature has solution for every problem and is the source of ultimate technology”.

The session wrapped up with a dynamic question-and-answer session, where participants actively interacted with the speaker, posing insightful questions and engaging in meaningful discussions.

A total of 52 students participated in the session. The event drew to a close at 04.30 p.m.

page_title: Guest Lecture on “Hidden Traps of Social Media” – 25-09-2024
text:
### Guest Lecture on “Hidden Traps of Social Media” – 25-09-2024

- September 29, 2024

The Women Empowerment Cell of AAA College of Engineering and Technology (AAACET) Sivakasi, organized an Guest Lecture on “Hidden Traps of Social Media” at our campus on 25.09.2024 from 11:00 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. at Sir Visvesvaraya Hall. The session was led by Mrs.R.Pon Meena, Inspector of Police,Vachakarapatti, Virudhunagar district, who shared valuable insights on traps of Social media. The program was Coordinated by Dr. R.Anitha, AP/Physics, and Mrs.V.Chandra, AP/EEE, with support from the convenor Dr.N.Thenmoezhi., AP/ECE & faculty members of the Women Empowerment Cell. The event began with a traditional lamp-lighting ceremony, symbolizing the enlightenment of knowledge The programme was attended by first, second & third year female students and began with the Thamizh Thai Vazhthu. Ms.R.Abirami.,III EEE welcomed the guest and the audience, and Ms.R.Nithya Lakshmi., III EEE introduced the guest speaker. Mrs.R.Ponmeena’s address focused on uncovering the often unnoticed risks and psychological pitfalls associated with heavy social media use. It emphasized the significant influence platforms like Instagram, Facebook, and Twitter have on behavior, mental health, relationships, and overall well-being. The lecture concluded by emphasizing the need for digital literacy and critical thinking when navigating social media. Users should be aware of the hidden traps, practice mindful usage, and take control of their digital environments to protect their mental health and well-being. The guest speaker encouraged the students to evaluate their relationship with social media and adopt healthier, more intentional habits. The event concluded with a vote of thanks by Ms.A.Priyanka., III EEE, and the National Anthem. The program was a great success.

page_title: Hands-on PLC Programming & Industrial Control on 27-08-2026
text:
### Hands-on PLC Programming & Industrial Control on 27-08-2026

- July 28, 2026

The Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering of AAA College of Engineering and Technology organized a Workshop on “Hands-on PLC Programming & Industrial Control” on 27.08.2026 (Thursday) from 1:30 p.m. to 4:40 p.m. at Thomas Alva Edison Hall, First Floor and Cambridge Block. The workshop was organized for the III Year EEE students with the objective of providing practical exposure to Programmable Logic Controllers (PLC) and their applications in industrial control and automation.

The session was conducted by Mr. P. Selva Vignesh, Alumnus (2015–2019 Batch – EEE) and Founder, Tech Solution, Sivakasi, who served as the Resource Person. His academic background in Electrical and Electronics Engineering and practical experience in the field of automation provided the students with valuable insights into PLC programming and industrial control applications.

During the workshop, the resource person introduced the students to the fundamentals of Programmable Logic Controllers (PLC) and their significance in modern industrial automation. He explained the basic architecture, working principles, programming concepts, and control logic associated with PLC-based systems. The students were provided with hands-on exposure to PLC programming and were guided in developing and implementing control logic for industrial applications. The practical demonstrations enabled the students to understand how PLCs are utilized for machine control, sequential operations, process automation, and industrial control.

The workshop aimed to bridge the gap between classroom learning and industrial requirements by providing students with practical knowledge of PLC programming and automation technologies. It helped the students understand the application of concepts related to Industrial Automation, Control Systems, Electrical Machines, Digital Electronics, and Industrial Instrumentation in real-time industrial environments. The session also emphasized the importance of developing practical programming and problem-solving skills for pursuing careers in industrial automation and control engineering.

The students actively participated in the hands-on activities and interacted with the resource person throughout the session. They raised questions related to PLC programming, control logic, automation applications, and industrial practices, and received practical guidance from the resource person. The interactive nature of the workshop helped the students strengthen their logical thinking, programming skills, and understanding of industrial control systems.

page_title: Pi (π) Day – International Mathematics Day on 14-03-2024
text:
### Pi (π) Day – International Mathematics Day on 14-03-2024

- March 15, 2024

The Department of Electronics Communication, AAA College of Engineering and Technology Sivakasi celebrated the Pi Day on today 14-03-2024 Thursday. Pi day Celebrated on March 14th (3/14),pays homage to the mathematical constant π (Pi) which represents the ratio of the circumference to its diameter.it was founded by Larry Shaw in 1988 .later ,in 2009 the United States house of representatives the designation of the pi day. A Guest Lecture by Dr. T. Senthil Professor & HOD/ECE is also arranged for discussing the 6 ways an ECE engineer uses the π in describing it’s applications.

- Calculation of Geo stationary orbit height and mean motion in the satellite communication.

- Signal analysis using Fourier series

page_title: PLACEMENT CELL MEETING & TRAINING ACTIVITIES FOR 2027 BATCH
text:
### PLACEMENT CELL MEETING & TRAINING ACTIVITIES FOR 2027 BATCH

- April 11, 2026

The Placement Cell of AAA College of Engineering and Technology organized an important meeting for all department placement coordinators and third-year students across all disciplines. The meeting was held on 8th April 2026 at 3:30 PM in the Kamaraj Auditorium .

This session was conducted with the objective of guiding students towards successful campus placements and preparing them for upcoming recruitment opportunities. The meeting emphasized the importance of early preparation, skill development, and active participation in placement activities.

Agenda of the Meeting

The following key topics were discussed during the session:

- Upcoming Companies & Placement Opportunities (2027 Batch): Students were informed about the expected companies and recruitment trends for the 2027 graduating batch.

- Placement Training Activities: Details about structured training programs, including aptitude, communication skills, and technical sessions, were shared.

- Mock Interview Sessions: The importance of mock interviews was highlighted to help students gain confidence and improve their performance in real interviews.

- Naukri Assessment Preparation: Guidance was provided on preparing for online assessments and improving performance in competitive recruitment tests.

- Coding Practice Platforms: Students were encouraged to regularly practice coding problems using platforms like LeetCode and HackerRank to strengthen their problem-solving skills.

The meeting served as a valuable platform to align students with placement expectations and motivate them to actively engage in training activities. The Placement Cell emphasized consistent effort, discipline, and skill enhancement as key factors for achieving placement success.

All participants were encouraged to utilize the available resources and stay committed to their preparation journey.

### Parents – Teachers Meeting on 13-09-2025

- September 17, 2025

The Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering organized a Parents–Teachers Meeting for all second-year and third-year students on 13.09.2025.

Mr. M. S. Kalyana Sundaram, Assistant Professor/EEE, welcomed the parents and initiated the session. Dr. C. Senthil Kumar, Professor and Head/EEE, addressed the gathering and presented the Vision and Mission of the Institution and the Department. He provided an overview of the faculty competency, highlighting the qualifications of members with Ph.D. degrees and those pursuing doctoral research. He also elaborated on the infrastructure facilities, laboratories, and resources available to support effective teaching–learning. Furthermore, he outlined the various co-curricular and extra-curricular activities organized by the Department and the Institution to enhance students’ overall development.

He highlighted the wide range of opportunities available in core electrical companies and emphasized their relevance to student placements. He also briefed the parents on the achievements of the Department, programs organized, and industry visits conducted during the academic year 2024–2025 (even semester). The proctors of each batch were formally introduced to the parents. Further, he instructed the faculty to reach out to the parents who could not attend the meeting and requested that updated mobile numbers and addresses be recorded in the proctor diary for effective communication.

In order to enhance student performance, the Head of the Department emphasized that students should avoid taking frequent leave from regular academic activities. He requested the parents to motivate and guide their wards to achieve better academic outcomes. He also informed them about the academic performance awards offered by the Institution. Students who secure a University rank in Anna University examinations will be refunded the full tuition fee paid for the course. Additionally, students who obtain a GPA of 9.0 or above in the end-semester examinations will be awarded a cash prize of ₹10,000/-.

He concluded his address by seeking the full cooperation of the parents for the enhancement of student progress and the growth of the Institution. He also expressed gratitude to all the parents for their active participation in the meeting. The parents appreciated the initiatives taken by the Department for the holistic development of the students and shared their valuable feedback on the activities conducted. The meeting concluded with a formal vote of thanks delivered by Mr. P. Nirmal Kumar, followed by refreshments.

### Workshop on Realization of Digital Logic Circuits in FPGA

- October 8, 2021

Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering is organizing a Three days Hands-on Workshop on “Realization of Digital Logic Circuits in FPGA” which will be held at AAA College of Engineering and Technology during 21 to 23 September 2017 . The objective of the workshop is to create awareness among the students about the design and development of digital logical circuits and its implementation in FPGA. Dr. Dhanabalan, Associate Professor, Department of ECE, will be the resource person for the workshop. He has more than 20 Year of Industrial and Teaching experience. Following topics will be covered during the workshop and hands-on training will be provided.

- Fundamentals of digital logic circuits

- Design of Combinational & Sequential Circuits

- Fundamentals of VerilogHDL Programming

- Building submodule’s in VerilogHDL

- Implementation of sequential circuits in FPGA

- Implementation of FSM’s in FPGA

text:
### From Campus to Career: TCNOM Engineers Recruitment Drive on 24-09-2026

AAA College of Engineering and Technology successfully conducted a Campus Recruitment Drive by TCNOM Engineers Pvt. Ltd., Chennai , on 24 September 2026 (Thursday) for final-year students of the Electrical and Electronics Engineering (EEE) and Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE) departments.

The recruitment drive provided students with a valuable opportunity to demonstrate their technical knowledge, skills, and professional abilities while exploring career opportunities with the organization. The selection process was conducted by Mr. Kiruba, HR , who interacted with the students and assessed their suitability for the available career opportunities. The students actively participated in the selection process and demonstrated enthusiasm, confidence, and commendable performance throughout the drive.

A total of 29 students were successfully selected , comprising 17 students from EEE and 12 students from ECE . As a mark of appreciation for their achievement, Dr. M. Sekar, Principal, AAA College of Engineering and Technology , presented offer letters to the selected students and congratulated them on their success.

The successful conduct of the recruitment drive was supported by the Management, Placement Director Mr. J. V. Saravana Lal, Placement Officer Dr. G. Jayahari Prabhu, Placement Coordinators of the concerned departments, and Placement Team members , whose dedicated efforts contributed to the smooth coordination of the recruitment activities.

The successful completion of the drive reflects the institution’s continued commitment to enhancing students’ employability, strengthening industry–institution collaboration, and creating meaningful career opportunities. The institution congratulates all the selected students and wishes them success in their professional journey.

### Parents Teachers Meeting for II & III Year EEE on 26-04-2025.

- April 30, 2025

The Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering conducted a Parents–Teachers meeting for all the second-year and the third-year students on 26.04.2025. Mrs.B.Sarojini AP/EEE welcomed all the parents who had gathered for the parents teacher meeting. Dr.C.Senthil Kumar, HoD/EEE, clearly explained the vision and mission of our institution and the department, and gave a brief introduction about the establishment of the college and department. He gave a detailed presentation on infrastructure details, guest lectures, and technical contests conducted under the department association. He gave a brief introduction about the department of EEE, profile of the head of the department, brief profile of the faculty working in the department with Ph.D, and faculty pursuing Ph.D. Infrastructure details such as laboratory facilities, classrooms, tutorial room, seminar hall, library and faculty room were clearly explained with photos and the softwares available in labs.

He informed about the plenty of opportunities available in the electrical core companies. He talked about the achievements, programs conducted, and the details of industry visits conducted in the academic year 2024-2025 (odd semester) and discussed the relevant importance to their placements. Proctors of each batch were introduced to all the parents. He informed the faculty to contact the students’ parents who were absent on the particular day. So he asked them to update the mobile number and address in the proctor diary.

In view of improving the students’ performance, the head of the department conveyed that the students should not often take leave from the regular classes. He informed the parents to motivate and concentrate their children to perform well in the university practical and the theory exams. The HoD informed about the academic performance awards. The student who secure Anna University rank will be refunded with the full tuition fees of the entire course of B.E Programme paid by him/her and also the student who secure more than 9 GPA in Anna University end semester examinations will be given a cash award of Rs.10,000/-.

The HoD concluded his speech by asking the full support and cooperation from the parents for the upliftment of the department and the college. Finally he thanked all the parents for attending the meeting. 32 parents attended the meeting. The parents appreciated the efforts taken by the department for the development of the students. The parents gave positive feedback on the activities of the department. Finally all the parents met the proctors and the program ended with the refreshment and tea.

page_title: Workshop on Productive Tools for Writing Journals & Articles
text:
### Workshop on Productive Tools for Writing Journals & Articles

- January 5, 2019

Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering organizes Two days National Level Workshop on Productive Tools for Writing Journals and Articles on 07/01/2019 & 08/01/2019 .

Traditionally an activity limited to pen and paper, the expansion of technology has enabled journaling to go digital. Journaling is one of the most useful personal development tools around. This workshop focuses to employ modern tools for writing journal, article and conference papers. This workshop covers hands on exercise on Microsoft Equation Editor, Microsoft Visio, LaTeX, Plagiarism checking etc.,

Microsoft Equation Editor is most desirable tool for writing scientific equations and formulae. Microsoft Visio has enormous features for drafting diagrams like electrical diagrams, block diagrams, 3D diagrams, flow charts, charts and maps. LaTeX is a document preparation system. It is widely used in academia for the communication and publication of research documents in journals, conferences and thesis writing. This workshop also covers the needs of modern tools for spell check, grammar check and plagiarism check. This program will motivate the participants to engage with their research activities using modern tools.

page_title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND MACHINE LEARNING LABORATORY
text:
### ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND MACHINE LEARNING LABORATORY

Name of the Lab | Artificial Intelligence and Machine learning Laboratory
Year of Establishment | 2025
Venue | Cambridge Block
Room No | 2221
Area | 83.61 Sq.m
Faculty In-charge | Mr.S. Manikandan, Assistant Professor/CSE
Lab Technician | Mrs.K.Divyabharathi

The Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AI & ML) Laboratory is a specialized computing facility established to support teaching, learning, research, and innovation in the domains of Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Data Analytics, Computer Vision, and Natural Language Processing. The laboratory provides students with a practical environment to design, develop, train, evaluate, and deploy intelligent systems capable of solving real-world engineering and societal problems.

The laboratory is equipped with 60 Intel Core (i7-6700) Processor systems connected through a high-speed Local Area Network (LAN) and supported by a centralized data center that enables efficient resource sharing and access to computational facilities. The laboratory operates in a fully air-conditioned environment with uninterrupted internet connectivity and a 20 KVA power backup system to ensure continuous academic and research activities.

To facilitate modern AI development, the laboratory provides access to industry-standard software platforms and frameworks including Python, Anaconda, Jupyter Notebook, TensorFlow, Keras, PyTorch, Scikit-learn, OpenCV, VirtualBox, and other advanced AI tools. These resources enable learners to perform data preprocessing, feature engineering, model development, performance evaluation, visualization, and deployment of machine learning and deep learning solutions.

The AI & ML Laboratory offers hands-on experience in supervised and unsupervised learning, neural networks, deep learning architectures, predictive analytics, computer vision systems, natural language processing applications, and intelligent automation. The facility also supports research and innovation activities in emerging areas such as Generative AI, Explainable AI, Reinforcement Learning, and Data-Driven Decision Making.

The primary objective of the laboratory is to bridge the gap between theoretical concepts and practical implementation by enabling students to develop intelligent solutions, analyze complex datasets, identify meaningful patterns, and build AI-enabled applications that address contemporary technological challenges.

The symposium aimed to enhance students’ technical knowledge and provide a common platform to showcase their innovative ideas and creativity in the field of Electrical and Electronics Engineering. The event began with the registration at 9.15 a.m., followed by a prayer song and the lighting of the kuthuvilakku, marking an auspicious start to the program. Ms. R. Nithyalakshmi (IV Year EEE) delivered the Welcome Address , warmly greeting the dignitaries, faculty members, and participants from various institutions. Dr. C. Senthil Kumar, Professor and Head of the Department of EEE , delivered the Inaugural Address , motivating students to explore new technological advancements and emphasizing the importance of hands-on learning and research-oriented thinking in the engineering domain. During the inauguration, the Department Magazine and Newsletter were formally introduced by the Chief Guests , marking a proud moment for the Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering as it showcased the achievements, innovations, and creative works of students and faculty members.

The chief guests of the event were Mr. S. Manimaran, B.E., Junior Engineer Grade–II, ESI Substation, Sivakasi , and Ms. M. Rashmika, B.E., EEE Alumna (2019–2023 Batch), Programmer Analyst, Cognizant Technology Solutions, Bangalore . Mr. S. Manimaran shared his professional experiences from the power sector, providing valuable insights into the operation and maintenance of substations, renewable energy integration, and the importance of safety and reliability in power systems. He encouraged the students to develop technical expertise and leadership qualities to succeed in the energy industry. Ms. M. Rashmika, an accomplished alumna of the EEE department, inspired the audience by narrating her journey from college life to the corporate world. She emphasized the importance of perseverance, communication skills, and adaptability in achieving professional success in the IT and technology sectors.

Following the inauguration, various technical events such as paper presentation, circuit debugging, project expo, and technical quiz were organized, providing an excellent opportunity for participants to exhibit their analytical and problem-solving skills. A total of 121 participants from several engineering colleges across Tamil Nadu and neighboring states took part in the symposium, making it a grand success. The participants actively engaged in competitions and interactive sessions, sharing their knowledge and gaining valuable exposure to emerging technologies.

### National Level Technical Symposium “Ampheroz’25” on 15-10-2025

A total of 121 participants from several engineering colleges across Tamil Nadu and neighboring states took part in the symposium, making it a grand success. The participants actively engaged in competitions and interactive sessions, sharing their knowledge and gaining valuable exposure to emerging technologies.

The Valedictory Function of AMPHEROZ’25 commenced at 4.00 p.m. , where certificates and prizes were distributed to the winners of the various events. The participants appreciated the hospitality, coordination, and smooth conduct of the program by the organizing team. Mr. K. M. Hari Prasath (IV Year EEE) delivered the Vote of Thanks , expressing heartfelt gratitude to the management, conveners, faculty coordinators, and student volunteers for their dedication and teamwork. He also extended his appreciation to the chief guests for their inspiring presence and valuable words of motivation.

The event concluded with the National Anthem at 4.35 p.m. , marking the end of a day filled with learning, innovation, and celebration of engineering talent.

### Guest Lecture on “Biomimicry-Science Innovation” on 28-02-2024

- March 2, 2024

In view of Science day celebration the Institution Innovation Council (IIC) of AAA College of Engineering organized a “ Guest Lecture on Biomimicry-Science Innovation” on 28.02.2024 . The Programme was conducted at Thomas Alva Edison hall, Cambridge block. Ms.S.Selvapriya, Third Year, Department of EEE, Student Co-ordinator IIC, extended a warm greeting to the delightful gathering followed by Dr.G.Vairamuthu, President, IIC, who gave a brief about the guest lecture conducted at AAACET.

Prof.Mr.M.Rajesh, Department of Zoology, The American College, President, Tamilnadu Science forum, Madurai was the resource person for this guest lecture. The Resource person focused on green building techniques that included biomimicry (how nature can be imitated in design) and how mimicry can help architects create a more efficient, sustainable and beautiful by learning from nature’s wisdom. In this presentation, he spoke about using nature in design-how the different parts of trees can be taken as an inspiration to create buildings. Objectives of conducting this lecture is to create products, processes, and systems new ways of living that solve our greatest design challenges sustainably and in solidarity with all life on earth. We can use biomimicry to not only learn from nature’s wisdom, but also heal ourselves and this planet in the process. . Benefit of conducting this lecture on biomimicry is to offer an empathetic, interconnected understanding of how life works and ultimately where we fit in. During the feedback session, the participants interacted with the resource person and clarified their queries regarding this biomimicry. Nearly 45 students and 10 faculty members were participated in this guest lecture. Ms.S.Mareeswari, Third Year, Department of EEE delivered the Vote of Thanks. Finally the Programme was ended with national anthem.

page_title: INAUGURAL CEREMONY OF SAEINDIA COLLEGIATE CLUB On 04-07-2026
text:
### INAUGURAL CEREMONY OF SAEINDIA COLLEGIATE CLUB On 04-07-2026

The Department of Mechanical Engineering, AAA College of Engineering and Technology (AAACET), Amathur, successfully inaugurated the SAEINDIA Collegiate Club on 04 July 2026 at the college campus with the enthusiastic participation of 53 SAE student members . The inauguration marked the establishment of a vibrant professional platform aimed at enhancing students’ technical competence, leadership abilities, innovation skills, and industry interaction through various SAEINDIA activities.

The inauguration ceremony was presided over by Dr. M. Sekar , Principal, AAACET, in the presence of Dr. S. S. Saravanakumar , Professor and Head, Department of Mechanical Engineering. The event was formally inaugurated by Dr. P. Baskara Sethupathi , Secretary, SAEINDIA Southern Section. In his inaugural address, he highlighted the significance of SAEINDIA in developing future engineers by providing opportunities to participate in technical competitions, workshops, industrial interactions, and professional networking. He emphasized that active involvement in SAEINDIA activities enables students to bridge the gap between classroom learning and industrial expectations.

Dr. Varunkumar , Chairman, SAEINDIA Southern Section – Madurai Division, interacted with the newly elected office bearers of the collegiate club and shared valuable suggestions for organizing technical events, promoting student leadership, and increasing participation in SAEINDIA initiatives. He motivated the students to make the club an active center for innovation, research, and professional development.

The programme was successfully coordinated by Mr. A. Vignesh Moorthy Pandian and Mr. M. Nagendran , Assistant Professors, Department of Mechanical Engineering. The inauguration concluded with a vote of thanks, marking the beginning of a new chapter for the SAEINDIA Collegiate Club at AAACET. The club is expected to provide students with extensive opportunities for technical learning, industrial exposure, teamwork, and leadership, thereby preparing them for successful careers in the automobile and allied engineering industries.

text:
### The Department of ECE Association Inauguration on 15-07-2026

- July 16, 2026

The Department of ECE of AAA College of Engineering and Technology in association with IETE Students forum organized *“ECE Association Inauguration and Guest lecture on Enhancing Research Visibility through Effective Scientific Writing”* on 15.07.2026. The Programme was conducted at Thomas Alva Edison Hall, Cambridge block AAACET. Ms.K.Rajakaleeswari III year ECE welcomed the gathering and Ms.M.Santhiya III ECE has given introduction about the chief guest.

Dr.B.Padmanaban, Professor and Head/ECE gave felicitation address. Office bearers for ECE association were introduced by association coordinator Mr.C.Shanmugaraja,AP/ ECE and association activities for the academic year 2026-2027 were planned.

Resource person for Association Inauguration and Guest lecture is

Dr.K.Senthilkannan,

Professor, Department of Research and Development, SMC,SIMATS, Chennai.

The resource person highlighted the importance of clear, concise, and well-structured scientific writing in improving the visibility and impact of research. Key topics included manuscript preparation, selecting suitable journals, ethical publishing practices, citation management, and strategies to increase research reach through indexing and academic networking platforms. The session was interactive, with participants actively engaging in discussions and clarifying their queries. The lecture enhanced participants understanding of effective scientific writing and motivated them to publish high-quality research in reputed journals.

Ms. Priyanka II year ECE gave vote of thanks. Finally the programme ended with National anthem.

Association coordinators Mr.C Shanmugaraja,AP/ECE and Mr.S.Prakash,AP/ ECE organized the event.

page_title: The seminar on How to Build AI Agents was held on 27-02-2026
text:
### The seminar on How to Build AI Agents was held on 27-02-2026

- February 28, 2026

The seminar on How to Build AI Agents was held on February 27th, 2026, at 10:00 AM and was conducted by Dr. S. Thayammal, Ph.D (BS-IITM), Director of Deep Dive Technologies . The session aimed to provide participants with an in-depth understanding of the process involved in creating intelligent AI agents, from initial planning to deployment and ongoing monitoring.

Dr. Thayammal began the seminar by emphasizing the importance of defining the purpose and goal of an AI agent. She explained that the first step in developing any AI system is to clearly understand what problem the agent is intended to solve. This involves identifying specific objectives and outcomes that the AI agent should achieve. For instance, an agent could be designed to automate customer support, provide real-time recommendations, or assist with complex data analysis. She highlighted that without a well-defined purpose, even the most advanced AI model would struggle to provide meaningful results.

Once the purpose is clear, Dr. Thayammal discussed the need to choose an appropriate framework or platform . She explained that frameworks like TensorFlow, PyTorch, and OpenAI APIs provide the foundational tools needed to build, train, and deploy AI agents. The choice of platform depends on several factors, including the type of AI agent, integration requirements, scalability, and available support for pre-trained models. Selecting the right framework ensures that the development process is efficient and that the agent can perform optimally in its intended environment.

The next critical step, according to Dr. Thayammal, is to select the brain of the AI agent , which could be a large language model (LLM) or a domain-specific model. She elaborated that the AI “brain” is responsible for understanding inputs, making decisions, and generating outputs. For general-purpose tasks, LLMs are highly effective due to their ability to understand and generate natural language. For specialized tasks, such as image recognition, predictive analytics, or financial forecasting, domain-specific models can offer higher precision and efficiency. The selection of the right model is crucial to ensure that the AI agent can meet its objectives effectively.

Following the selection of the model, the seminar covered the importance of defining tools and actions . Dr. Thayammal explained that an AI agent relies on a set of tools and actions to interact with its environment and perform its tasks. This may include APIs for accessing external data, automation scripts for executing tasks, or integration with other software systems. Clear definition of actions helps prevent errors and ensures the agent behaves in a controlled and predictable manner while interacting with users or other systems.

Dr. Thayammal then elaborated on developing the workflow and logic of an AI agent. This involves mapping out how the agent processes inputs, makes decisions, and executes actions.

This may include APIs for accessing external data, automation scripts for executing tasks, or integration with other software systems. Clear definition of actions helps prevent errors and ensures the agent behaves in a controlled and predictable manner while interacting with users or other systems. Dr. Thayammal then elaborated on developing the workflow and logic of an AI agent. This involves mapping out how the agent processes inputs, makes decisions, and executes actions.

She highlighted the importance of creating structured decision-making processes, which could be implemented through decision trees, reinforcement learning loops, or other algorithmic workflows. Effective workflow design ensures that the agent performs tasks efficiently, responds accurately to different scenarios, and can handle exceptions without failure.

Finally, the seminar addressed deployment and monitoring . Dr. Thayammal explained that once an AI agent is developed, it must be deployed on suitable servers or cloud platforms, where it can operate in real-time or batch modes depending on the application. Continuous monitoring is essential to track performance, detect errors, and gather data for improvement. She stressed that AI agents are not static; their effectiveness can be enhanced over time through iterative updates, performance tuning, and adaptation to changing requirements.

The seminar concluded with a discussion on the dynamic nature of AI development and the importance of ongoing learning and experimentation. Participants gained a thorough understanding of the practical steps involved in building AI agents, from conceptualization and model selection to workflow design, deployment, and continuous improvement. Dr. Thayammal’s insights provided valuable guidance for both beginners and professionals interested in AI agent development, emphasizing that successful AI implementation combines careful planning, technical skill, and continuous adaptation.

Overall, the seminar was highly informative, offering detailed guidance on creating AI agents that are functional, efficient, and capable of solving real-world problems. Participants left with practical knowledge, actionable steps, and a strong foundation for embarking on their own AI projects.

page_title: A New Chapter Begins: Induction Ceremony for M.E. – CSE (2025–2027)
text:
### A New Chapter Begins: Induction Ceremony for M.E. – CSE (2025–2027)

- College Announcements , M.E ( CSE )

- September 4, 2025

The AAA College of Engineering and Technology organized its first-ever Induction Programme for the newly introduced M.E. – Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) course on 3rd September 2025 (Wednesday) at the Sir Visvesvaraya Seminar Hall, Cambridge Block . The event was conducted between 10:00 A.M. and 11.000 A.M.

Significance of the Event

This programme was historic as it marked the introduction of the M.E. – CSE course for the first time in the institution’s history . It was designed to orient the students of the 2025–2027 batch and provide them with a strong foundation for their academic and professional journey.

Event Progression

Opening Ceremony

- The event commenced with the rendition of Tamilthai Vazhthu , invoking cultural pride and tradition.

- This was followed by the Lighting of the Kuthuvilakku , symbolizing knowledge and wisdom. The lamp was lit by Dr. M. Sekar (Principal), Dr. J. Hemalatha (HOD – CSE-PG), Dr. P. Senthil Pandian (Academic Coordinator), and Dr. P. Devabalan (Dean – R&D) .

Welcome and Programme Highlights

- Dr. J. Hemalatha , HOD of CSE-PG, delivered an address explaining the significance of the newly introduced M.E. – CSE course and elaborated on the 2025 Regulation framework .

Principal’s Address

- Dr. M. Sekar , Principal, motivated students to explore their future career pathways after completing M.E. – whether in the teaching profession or in the software industry , urging them to make informed and impactful choices.

Dean’s Address

- Dr. P. Devabalan , Dean – Research and Development, highlighted the importance of research in postgraduate education. He encouraged students to involve themselves in projects, publications, and innovation-driven learning .

Vote of Thanks

- The programme concluded with a Vote of Thanks delivered by Dr. P. Senthil Pandian, Academic Coordinator , who expressed gratitude to the dignitaries, faculty members, and students for their active participation and support.

Dignitaries Present

The programme was presided over by eminent members of the management and faculty:

- Dr. M. Sekar – Principal

- Dr. J. Hemalatha, M.E., Ph.D. – HOD / CSE-PG

- Dr.P.Devabalan, M.E., Ph.D.,(PDF) – DEAN – Research and Development

- Dr. P.Senthil Pandian , M.E., Ph.D. – Academic Coordinator

- Dr. J.Chandra Priya, M.E., Ph.D.

Student Orientation

The induction programme provided an overview of:

- Academic regulations, curriculum, and evaluation methods.

- Research prospects and funded project opportunities.

text:
### Funding Opportunities for Early Stage Entrepreneur on 01-11-2023

The Institution’s Innovation Council (IIC) and Entrepreneurship Development Cell (EDC) , organized a Guest Lecture titled ‘ Funding Opportunities for Early Stage Entrepreneur .’ The session took place on November 01, 2023, at 03.00 p.m.

Dr. G. Vairamuthu, President of IIC, presided over the event. The session commenced with a welcome address from Mr. M. Sivasankar, EDC Coordinator.

Mrs. D. Chellathai, Joint Manager at Bank of Baroda, Sivakasi, served as the resource person for the session. She initiated the session by highlighting her expertise and experience in the field of entrepreneurship and funding opportunities. After that, she discussed various funding options available for early-stage entrepreneurs, such as angel investors, venture capitalists, crowdfunding, grants, and government schemes. She also explained the differences between equity funding and debt financing, outlining the pros and cons of each. Furthermore, she emphasized the importance of networking and building relationships within the entrepreneurial community. Finally, she discussed how access to funding can help entrepreneurs scale their businesses, invest in research and development, and expand their market reach.

The session wrapped up with a dynamic question-and-answer session, where participants actively interacted with the speaker, posing insightful questions and engaging in meaningful discussions.

A total of 435 students participated in the session. The event drew to a close at 04.30 p.m

page_title: Introductory Session on AAACET-Tenova Hackathon on 26-09-2025
text:
### Introductory Session on AAACET-Tenova Hackathon on 26-09-2025

- December 4, 2025

The Department of Artificial Intelligence and Data Science conducted “Introductory Session on AAACET-Tenova Hackathon,” on September 26, 2025, at Sir C V Raman Hall, Third Floor, Cambridge Block. The event aimed to nurture thinking among students and provide practical knowledge on the processes involved in a hackathon.

The seminar featured Mr. Ajmeer Kaja Mohideen, Director of Operations. Drawing from his professional expertise, they delivered an insightful address covering multiple aspects of innovation, ideas, and procedures in the Tenova Hackathon. He explained the importance of the Python programming language and its various libraries, highlighting how they are widely used in real-time applications. Furthermore, he informed the students about an upcoming hackathon to be conducted exclusively for them, and clearly explained the rules and regulations for participation.

The second session was led by Mr. Mohamed Arshath, Chief Architect, who guided the students on how to approach a hackathon step by step. Starting from the basics, he explained the methods to participate effectively and how to proceed to the next level. His talk motivated the students to take part in the upcoming hackathon with confidence and enthusiasm. The sessions were not only informative but also highly engaging, sparking curiosity and enthusiasm among participants. By shedding light on real-world applications of Python, the importance of algorithms, and the strategic approach to hackathons.

The announcement of the upcoming Tenova Hackathon added a layer of excitement, encouraging students to apply the insights gained and actively participate. The clear explanation of rules and guidance on preparation helped demystify the process, making it accessible even to beginners. The presence of seasoned professional, Mr. Iham Khan, Advisor, as the chief guest, served as a source of inspiration, bridging the gap between academic learning and industry expectations. Overall, the event fostered a spirit of innovation and collaboration, empowering students to think creatively and work towards impactful solutions. It was a valuable initiative that not only enhanced technical knowledge but also boosted confidence, teamwork, and problem-solving skills—qualities essential for success in any field.

### National Level Technical Symposium VALIANT 2K24 on 20-03-2024

- March 25, 2024

The Department of Electronics Communication, AAA College of Engineering and Technology Sivakasi organized National Level Technical Symposium VALIANT 2K24 on 20-03-2024. The symposium witnessed huge response from the student community with 127 registered student’s participation in physical and 6 students in online mode from 14 colleges. text:
### Awareness Programme on “Hidden Traps of social Media” – 25-09-2024

- September 27, 2024

The Women Empowerment Cell of AAA College of Engineering and Technology (AAACET) Sivakasi, organized an Guest Lecture on “Hidden Traps of Social Media” at our campus on 25.09.2024 from 11:00 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. at Sir Visvesvaraya Hall. The session was led by Mrs.R.Pon Meena, Inspector of Police,Vachakarapatti, Virudhunagar district, who shared valuable insights on traps of Social media.

The program was Coordinated by Dr. R.Anitha, AP/Physics, and Mrs.V.Chandra, AP/EEE, with support from the convenor Dr.N.Thenmoezhi., AP/ECE & faculty members of the Women Empowerment Cell. The event began with a traditional lamp-lighting ceremony, symbolizing the enlightenment of knowledge The programme was attended by first, second & third year female students and began with the Thamizh Thai Vazhthu. Ms.R.Abirami., III EEE welcomed the guest and the audience, and Ms.R.Nithya Lakshmi., III EEE introduced the guest speaker.

Mrs.R.Ponmeena’s address focused on uncovering the often unnoticed risks and psychological pitfalls associated with heavy social media use. It emphasized the significant influence platforms like Instagram, Facebook, and Twitter have on behavior, mental health, relationships, and overall well-being. The lecture concluded by emphasizing the need for digital literacy and critical thinking when navigating social media. Users should be aware of the hidden traps, practice mindful usage, and take control of their digital environments to protect their mental health and well-being.

The guest speaker encouraged the students to evaluate their relationship with social media and adopt healthier, more intentional habits. The event concluded with a vote of thanks by Ms.A.Priyanka., III EEE, and the National Anthem. The program was a great success .

text:
### Association valedictory and inauguration – CRYPTNOVA on 04-08-2026

- August 19, 2026

The Department of Computer Science and Engineering (Cyber Security), AAA College of Engineering and Technology, in association with CRYPTNOVA , successfully organized the Association Valedictory and Inauguration on 04th July 2026 at 10:00 A.M. in Thomas Alva Edison Hall, Cambridge Block . The event marked the official launch of the department association for the academic year with the objective of encouraging students to actively participate in technical, professional, and co-curricular activities.

The programme commenced with a warm welcome address by Ms.Rithsia, III Year , Department of CSE (Cyber Security), She welcomed the Chief Guest, management members, Head of the Department, faculty members, and students.

This was followed by a felicitation address by Dr. P. Elamparithi , Associate Professor and Head, Department of CSE (Cyber Security). In his address he highlighted the objectives of CRYPTNOVA in promoting technical excellence and professional development. He encouraged students to actively participate in the association’s activities and make the best use of the opportunities provided for learning and innovation.

The introduction of the Chief Guest was given by Mr. Balapragadhish , III year, who briefed the audience on the professional background, industry experience, and technical expertise of the resource person.

This was followed by the inauguration of CRYPTNOVA , the Cyber Security Association. The event was graced by the Chief Guest, Mr. Dharrun Kannan, Quarksek Technology Pvt. Ltd., Bangalore , who inaugurated the association and addressed the gathering. In his inspiring speech, delivered an insightful guest lecture on “Recent Trends in Cyber Security with Artificial Intelligence.” He highlighted the growing role of AI in threat detection, malware analysis, incident response, and cyber defense, while encouraging students to develop industry-relevant skills and stay updated with emerging technologies in the rapidly evolving cybersecurity landscape.

page_title: A NATIONAL LEVEL TECHNICAL HACKATHON NEURAHACK 2K25 on 16-10-2025
text:
### A NATIONAL LEVEL TECHNICAL HACKATHON NEURAHACK 2K25 on 16-10-2025

- October 17, 2025

Organized by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering Date: October 16, 2025 Venue: Kamarajar Auditorium, AAA College of Engineering and Technology, Amathur, Sivakasi

About the Event

The Department of Computer Science and Engineering of AAA College of Engineering and Technology successfully organized NEURAHACK 2K25 , a National Level Technical Hackathon , on October 16, 2025 . The event aimed to bring together passionate and innovative students from across the country to collaborate, ideate, and develop advanced technology-driven solutions for real-world challenges.

The hackathon served as a vibrant platform to promote innovation, problem-solving, and teamwork among aspiring technologists while fostering interaction with industry professionals and academic mentors.

A total of 50 teams from various colleges participated, comprising more than 100 students , reflecting the growing enthusiasm for technical innovation among young engineers.

Event Proceedings

The event commenced with registration at 8:30 A.M. , followed by an assembly in the Kamarajar Auditorium . The opening ceremony began with the Tamilthai Vazhthu and the lighting of the ceremonial lamp , symbolizing the spirit of enlightenment and innovation.

The Welcome Address was delivered by Ms. N. Basheer Nisha Bagam (III Year CSE) , who warmly greeted the dignitaries, faculty members, and participants. She highlighted the objective of NEURAHACK 2K25 and the significance of hackathons in fostering real-world problem-solving skills among students.

The gathering was further addressed by Dr. J. Hemalatha , Professor & Head of the Department of CSE, who emphasized creative learning, collaboration, and innovation in engineering education. Dr. M. Sekar , Principal of the institution, encouraged students to embrace challenges as opportunities for growth and to transform their ideas into impactful solutions.

Chief Guest and Felicitation

The event’s Chief Guest , Mr. Visakh ST, Chief Technology Officer of Simplify3X Software Pvt. Ltd. , was introduced by Ms. S. Muthu Nandhini (III Year CSE) , who highlighted his remarkable achievements and contributions to technology and innovation.

In his keynote address, the Chief Guest motivated participants to leverage emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain, and Cloud Computing, while focusing on skill enhancement and continuous learning. His insights on innovation and industry expectations greatly inspired the participants.

A memento was presented to the Chief Guest as a token of appreciation for his presence and contribution.

Hackathon Highlights

The hackathon officially began at 11:00 A.M. , with 50 teams comprising over 100 students enthusiastically engaging in innovative project development. The participants demonstrated creativity, technical proficiency, and teamwork under the mentorship of faculty members from the Department of CSE.
